syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Government Policies and Interventions

title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: Environmental outcomes of BioE3 Policy
summary: In a written Rajya Sabha reply, the Minister of State for Science & Technology, Dr. Jitendra Singh, detailed the environmental outcomes of the BioE3 (Biotechnology for Economy, Environment and Employment) Policy implemented by the Department of Biotechnology. The reply highlighted the 'Sujivika' digital portal for tracking biotech imports, support for bio-refinery and waste-to-value projects, and interventions like Sunderbans ecosystem restoration, alternatives to single-use plastics, and sustainable aviation fuel production. These efforts aim to reduce fossil-fuel dependency, cut greenhouse gas emissions, and advance India's circular bioeconomy and Net Zero commitments.

title: “EDUCATION AND HOUSING SCHEMES FOR STS IN KERALA”
summary: In a Lok Sabha reply, MoS Tribal Affairs Durgadas Uikey detailed the income-eligibility limits under five central ST scholarship schemes (Pre-Matric, Post-Matric, Top Class, NFST, NOS) and NSTFDC concessional loans, along with housing support under PM JANMAN/PMAY-G for PVTGs and Kerala's own LIFE Mission and state scholarship schemes. He noted that a proposal to revise the income ceilings is under EFC appraisal for FY2026-31, pending Department of Expenditure approval.

title: Dr. Padma Gurmet Conferred UT Ladakh State Award 2025 for Exemplary Service to Sowa-Rigpa Medicine
summary: Dr. Padma Gurmet, Director of the National Institute of Sowa-Rigpa (NISR), Leh, has been conferred the UT Ladakh State Award for 2025 for his contribution to preserving, promoting and developing the Sowa-Rigpa system of medicine. The award was presented by Lieutenant Governor Vinai Kumar Saxena at a ceremony honouring 36 individuals for the years 2022-2025 across various fields.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Government Policies and Interventions

title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: PRIVATE COMPANIES IN SPACE SECTOR
summary: In a written Rajya Sabha reply, Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh stated that around 440 space technology startups are registered under the DPIIT Start-up India Portal, and IN-SPACe has granted 113 authorisations to 52 Non-Government Entities (NGEs), including 18 startups, for various space activities. He also disclosed that private Indian companies are expected to launch 2 commercial rockets in FY 2026-27 and more than 6 in FY 2027-28, subject to IN-SPACe's launch manifest approval.

title: STRENGTHENING PM-JANMAN for PVTGs
summary: The Union Minister of State for Tribal Affairs informed Lok Sabha about the progress of PM-JANMAN, a mission launched by the PM for socio-economic development of 75 Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs) across 18 states and one UT. The scheme covers 11 interventions across 9 line ministries including housing, roads, water, health, education, electrification and telecom connectivity, with state-wise and ministry-wise progress data given as on 30.06.2026. Chhattisgarh has 191 sanctioned Anganwadi Centres, all operationalized, under the Ministry of Women and Child Development's Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0.

title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: APPLICATIONS OF SPACE TECHNOLOGY
summary: In a written Rajya Sabha reply, the Department of Space detailed major satellite missions launched in the last three years (Chandrayaan-3, Aditya-L1, XPoSat, SPADEX, NISAR, GSAT-7R) and applications of space technology in agriculture, disaster management, governance and satellite communication. It also listed high-impact use cases identified for Non-Government Entities via IN-SPACe, and outlined upcoming missions including Gaganyaan, Venus Orbiter Mission, Chandrayaan-4 and Chandrayaan-5/LUPEX.

title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: SUPPORT TO SPACE STARTUPS
summary: In a written Rajya Sabha reply on 13 August 2026, Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh detailed government support to India's space startups: about 440 space-tech startups are registered on the DPIIT Start-up India Portal, and IN-SPACe has granted 113 authorisations to 52 Non-Government Entities, of which 18 are startups. The reply listed year-wise facilitation (launch slots, testing access) provided since 2022 to startups like Skyroot, Agnikul, Pixxel, Dhruva Space and others, and disclosed IN-SPACe's fund disbursements (Seed Fund, Venture Capital Funds, Technology Adoption Fund, SBaaS, Common Technical Facilities) totalling about Rs 200 crore over five years as of 31 July 2026.

title: Implementation of Adi Karmayogi Abhiyan
summary: The Ministry of Tribal Affairs informed Parliament that Phase-I of the Adi Karmayogi Abhiyan has built a nationwide capacity-building framework covering about one lakh tribal villages across 30 States/UTs. Key achievements include mobilising around 15 lakh Adi Karmayogis through a cascading training structure, approving 62,187 Tribal Village Vision 2030 Plans via Gram Sabhas, and establishing 56,422 Adi Sewa Kendras as village-level single-window facilitation centres supported by Adi Karmayogi Volunteers.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Devolution of powers and finances to local bodies, Panchayati Raj (PESA)

title: Mobile and Internet Connectivity in Tribal Areas
summary: In a Lok Sabha reply, the Minister of State for Tribal Affairs stated that the Digital Bharat Nidhi (DBN), under the Department of Telecommunications, has funded mobile connectivity projects covering uncovered and tribal-dominated villages nationwide, including in Sasaram Lok Sabha Constituency (Kaimur and Rohtas districts, Bihar). As of 30 June 2026, of 3,764 total villages in the constituency, only 12 remain uncovered by 4G, and the constituency has 4,377 4G and 1,110 5G BTS towers. The reply also gave state-wise DBN/DAPST fund disbursement figures for 2021-26 (total Rs. 2,183.10 crore) and reiterated that PM-JANMAN's 4G saturation scheme aims to provide telecom connectivity to uncovered villages/habitations, including PVTG areas, within a three-year mission period.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Government Policies and Interventions

title: STATUS OF VAN DHAN VIKAS KENDRA CLUSTERS
summary: The Ministry of Tribal Affairs informed Parliament that 4,712 Van Dhan Vikas Kendras (VDVKs), covering 12.94 lakh beneficiaries, have been sanctioned across 28 States/UTs with Rs. 642.19 crore under PMJVM and PM-JANMAN, of which 3,406 are operational. It detailed fund flow mechanisms including the Treasury Single Account system, MSP-based revolving funds for Minor Forest Produce procurement (with Rs. 2.50 crore released to Meghalaya in FY2025-26), and Chhattisgarh's cumulative Rs. 153.66 crore revolving fund since 2013-14 procuring MFPs worth Rs. 467 crore.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Government Policies and Interventions

title: STATUS OF EMRSs
summary: The Union Minister of Tribal Affairs, Shri Jual Oram, informed the Lok Sabha that 728 Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRSs) have been approved nationwide, of which 508 are functional with 156,593 students enrolled in academic year 2025-26. In Telangana, all 23 sanctioned EMRSs are functional, enrolling 10,199 students. The statement also detailed quality-enhancement measures including smart classrooms, science/computer labs, vocational training, and cultural preservation initiatives like Tribal Corners and regional language teachers.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Government Policies and Interventions

title: Semiconductor and AI Revolution
summary: This PIB backgrounder outlines India's dual push in semiconductors and Artificial Intelligence as India marks its 80th Independence Day. It details Semicon India 1.0 (₹76,000 crore) and the newly approved Semicon 2.0 (₹1,27,500 crore, approved July 2026) covering chip design, fabrication, packaging, equipment, materials, R&D and talent, with 12 semiconductor projects worth over ₹1.64 lakh crore approved across six states and three plants already in commercial production. It also details the IndiaAI Mission (~₹10,372 crore outlay), covering compute infrastructure (45,000+ GPUs), 20 selected indigenous foundation AI models, the AI Kosh data/model repository, 58 approved AI Centres of Excellence, Responsible AI projects, and India's global AI standing including the India AI Impact Summit 2026 and Pax Silica coalition.

title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: PERFORMANCE OF CPGRAMS

ministry.name: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions

summary: In a written reply to the Rajya Sabha, the Minister of State for Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, Dr. Jitendra Singh, provided Ministry/Department-wise data on grievances received, disposed of and pending on the CPGRAMS portal for FY 2023-24, 2024-25 and 2025-26 (as on 05-08-2026). The reply also referenced the Comprehensive Guidelines for Effective Redressal of Public Grievances issued on 23 August 2024, which prescribe a 21-day grievance redressal timeline, and noted that a Feedback Call Centre has been operational since July 2022 to independently assess citizen satisfaction with grievance resolution.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Citizens' Charters and Grievance Redressal Mechanisms

title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: iGOT MISSION KARMAYOGI IN WEST BENGAL

ministry.name: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions

summary: In a written Rajya Sabha reply, Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh stated that 90,276 civil servants from West Bengal have been onboarded onto the iGOT Karmayogi digital learning platform, though the West Bengal government has not yet signed the tripartite MoU under Mission Karmayogi. Eight draft Capacity Building Plans have been prepared for the state's priority departments, and 10,493 course completions have been recorded by West Bengal learners out of over 5,600 courses available on the platform. DoPT, the Capacity Building Commission, and Karmayogi Bharat are extending handholding support to the state, including nodal officers for coordination.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Government Policies and Interventions
GS Paper 3 - Role of e-governance in public administration

title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: ZERO LITIGATION PENSION ECOSYSTEM

ministry.name: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions

summary: In a written Rajya Sabha reply, Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh described government efforts to build a 'zero litigation' pension ecosystem, highlighting the 2nd National Workshop on Pension Litigation organised by the Department of Pension and Pensioners' Welfare (DoPPW). The workshop launched a Compendium of case laws and an explanatory flyer on best practices in pension litigation, alongside 'Special Campaign 3' aimed at resolving long-pending pension grievances. The reply also referenced Pension Adalats, Inter-Ministerial Review Meetings, and the CCS (Pension) Rules 2021, which replaced the 1972 Rules and eased eligibility conditions for family pensioners including divorced and disabled daughters under Rule 50.

title: Empowering Youth, Transforming India
summary: This PIB backgrounder consolidates a decade-plus of Indian government initiatives for youth empowerment across education, skilling, employment, sports, health and civic participation, framed under the 'Amrit Peedhi' (nectar generation) working toward 'Viksit Bharat@2047'. Key highlights include the Mera Yuva Bharat (MY Bharat) platform with 2.22 crore registered youth, NEP 2020-driven education reforms, skilling missions like PMKVY and PM-SETU, sports infrastructure under Khelo India and TOPS, and health initiatives like Tele-MANAS and Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan. The release presents extensive statistics comparing 2014 baselines with 2025-26 achievements to demonstrate transformation in youth development outcomes.

title: Expanding the Development Horizon
summary: A PIB backgrounder dated 13 August 2026 consolidates cumulative achievements across rural and tribal development schemes in India, covering fiscal devolution, basic services, infrastructure, livelihoods, financial inclusion, social security and targeted tribal/SC interventions. It highlights that Gram Panchayat fiscal transfers rose from ₹2.36 lakh crore under the 15th Finance Commission to ₹4.35 lakh crore under the 16th Finance Commission, and that flagship programmes such as Jal Jeevan Mission, Swachh Bharat-Grameen, PMAY-G, PMGSY, DAY-NRLM and PM-JANMAN have expanded coverage substantially since 2014-15. The document also details growth in financial inclusion (Jan Dhan, MUDRA, PM SVANidhi), social security (NPS, Atal Pension Yojana, PMJJBY/PMSBY) and tribal/SC welfare schemes (PM-JVM, PM-JUGA, PM-AJAY, EMRS, PM-YASASVI).

title: National Biodiversity Authority releases Rs. 15.52 crore ABS Proceeds from Mustard Genetic Resources

ministry.name: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

summary: The National Biodiversity Authority (NBA) has disbursed Rs. 15.52 crore in Access and Benefit Sharing (ABS) proceeds collected from M/s. Pioneer Overseas Corporation, which developed ten commercial mustard hybrid varieties using India's biological resources. Since the parental lines were sourced from intermediaries rather than identifiable farmers, an Expert Committee devised a formula distributing the funds among 26 State Biodiversity Boards and 3 Union Territory Biodiversity Councils based on each region's mustard cultivation area, using ICAR-IIRMR data. Rajasthan received the largest share (Rs. 6.43 crore, ~42% of cultivation), followed by Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh. NBA has released Rs. 182.5 crore in total ABS funds to date, with Rs. 116.22 crore disbursed in the last 12 months.

title: Prime Minister shares a Sanskrit Subhashitam, highlighting determination, perseverance, and continuous effort in overcoming life's challenges
summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi shared a Sanskrit Subhashitam (verse of wisdom) on social media platform X on 13 August 2026, emphasizing determination, perseverance and courage as means to overcome life's adversities. The verse conveys that a person with resolve is never defeated by fate but achieves success through continuous effort.

title: The New Era of Indian Agriculture and Allied Sectors
summary: This PIB backgrounder presents a comprehensive overview of transformation in India's agriculture and allied sectors over the past decade, covering rising GVA, foodgrain and horticulture production, farmer welfare schemes (PM-KISAN, PMFBY, MSP, KCC), sustainable farming initiatives (Soil Health Cards, PKVY, Natural Farming Mission, PM-KUSUM), food security (NFSA, SARTHAK PDS), market linkages (e-NAM, AIF), food processing reforms (PLISFPI, PMKSY), agricultural exports, digital agriculture initiatives, and growth in livestock, dairy and fisheries sectors. It highlights India's position as the world's largest milk producer and significant growth across allied sectors like fisheries and poultry.

title: Third Meeting of Hindi Advisory Committee of Ministry of Ayush Held in New Delhi
summary: The third meeting of the Hindi Advisory Committee of the Ministry of Ayush was held in New Delhi under the chairmanship of MoS Prataprao Jadhav, attended by MPs, the Ayush Secretary, and committee members. The meeting focused on promoting the use of Hindi in official work, publications, and public outreach for the Ayush sector, and the Ministry's Hindi house journal 'Apratim Ayush' was released. Discussions centered on making Ayush-related research and schemes accessible in Hindi and other Indian languages.

title: BHARAT TAXI ROLL OUT
summary: Bharat Taxi, a cooperative-led app-based mobility platform run by Sahakar Taxi Cooperative Limited (STCL), a multistate cooperative society, has been officially rolled out in Delhi-NCR, Gujarat, Maharashtra and Rajasthan, with phased expansion to other cities like Lucknow, Chandigarh, Jaipur and Pune. As of 4 August 2026, it has 8.48 lakh registered drivers (Sarathis), 44.27 lakh customers, facilitates 11,106 daily rides, and has generated ₹83.70 crore in cumulative driver earnings. STCL has also signed an MoU with the West Bengal government to support its Yatri Sathi platform through driver enrolment, cooperative membership and welfare initiatives. This information was shared by Union Home and Cooperation Minister Amit Shah in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 3 - Role of cooperatives in inclusive economic development

title: NEW COURSES AT TRIBHUVAN COOPERATIVE UNIVERSITY (TSU)
summary: The Ministry of Cooperation informed Rajya Sabha that Tribhuvan Sahkari University (TSU) launched three new MBA programmes in 2025-26 — Cooperative Management, Cooperative Banking and Finance, and Agribusiness Management. The university has also designed five certificate courses for professional management of cooperative societies (covering PACS, fisheries cooperatives, dairy cooperatives, DCCB board leadership, and cybersecurity for cooperative banks), to be rolled out in 2026-27. Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Amit Shah gave this information in a written reply.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Government Policies and Interventions

title: AVAILABILITY OF QUALITY SEEDS AND FARMERS' SELF-RELIANCE THROUGH BBSSL
summary: The Ministry of Cooperation informed the Rajya Sabha that Bhartiya Beej Sahakari Samiti Limited (BBSSL), an apex cooperative body set up under the MSCS Act 2002, has introduced 124 varieties of seeds across 18 crops under the 'Bharat Beej' brand. In FY 2025-26, BBSSL produced 75,535 metric tonnes of seeds through associated farmers, and it has also launched a conservation programme for traditional indigenous seed varieties in Uttarakhand. The initiative aims to expand domestic seed production, conserve genetic resources, and reduce India's dependence on imported seeds.

title: Affordable and Accessible Healthcare for All
summary: This PIB backgrounder consolidates 12 years of India's health sector achievements, covering Ayushman Bharat's insurance coverage and digital mission, the National Health Mission's maternal-child health and disease control programmes, affordable medicine schemes like Jan Aushadhi and AMRIT, digital health tools like eSanjeevani and Tele-MANAS, and expansion of medical education infrastructure. Key figures include over 45.5 crore Ayushman Cards issued, maternal mortality declining to 87 per 1,00,000 live births, and medical colleges more than doubling from 387 to 818. The release also highlights India's exit from WHO's malaria high-burden group and integration of AYUSH systems into mainstream healthcare.

title: OBJECTIVE OF THE RANKING FRAMEWORK FOR COOPERATIVE SOCIETIES
summary: The Ministry of Cooperation informed the Rajya Sabha that a Ranking Framework for primary cooperative societies, launched on 24 January 2025, uses the National Cooperative Database (NCD) to rank societies sector-wise and State/district/block-wise across 12 sectors. State/UT Registrars of Cooperative Societies use the NCD portal to assess societies on five parameters—audit compliance, operational activities, financial performance, infrastructure, and basic identity information—out of a total of 100 marks. The framework aims to enhance transparency, efficiency, credibility, and competitiveness among cooperatives and enable dissemination of best practices from top performers.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Role of institutions and bodies in economic development

title: BENCHMARKS FOR ORGANIC PRODUCTS OF NCOL
summary: National Cooperative Organics Limited (NCOL) markets certified organic products under the 'Bharat Organics' brand through e-commerce, modern retail, cooperative outlets (Safal/Mother Dairy, NAFED, NCCF) and a D2C portal. It complies with National Programme for Organic Production (NPOP) standards notified by APEDA, sourcing from certified farmer groups/ICS, conducting mandatory lab testing for pesticide residues, and has signed MoUs with 28 States/UTs to promote organic cooperative farming. This was stated by Union Home and Cooperation Minister Amit Shah in a written reply in Rajya Sabha.

title: BHARAT TAXI - COOPERATIVE-MODEL MOBILITY PLATFORM
summary: Bharat Taxi, a cooperative-led digital cab-hailing platform run by Sahakar Taxi Cooperative Limited (STCL), a multistate cooperative society, has been launched in Delhi-NCR, Gujarat, Maharashtra and Rajasthan. As of 04.08.2026, it has 8.48 lakh registered drivers (Sarathis) and 44.27 lakh registered customers. The platform follows a zero-commission, subscription-based model with transparent fares and driver welfare measures, and receives no government financial support, as stated by Union Cooperation Minister Amit Shah in a Rajya Sabha written reply.

title: DIGITAL TECHNOLOGY IN THE COOPERATIVE SECTOR
summary: The Ministry of Cooperation has outlined multiple digital initiatives undertaken over the last three years to modernize India's cooperative sector under the 'Sahkar Se Samriddhi' vision. Key achievements include computerization of 63,686 Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) onto ERP-based software, with 54,707 declared e-PACS and over 51.58 crore digital transactions recorded. Other initiatives include computerization of Registrar of Cooperative Societies (RCS) offices, Agriculture and Rural Development Banks (ARDBs), the National Cooperative Database (NCD) covering 8.6 lakh cooperatives, and a Cooperative Ranking Framework launched in January 2025.

title: COORDINATION BETWEEN NCOL AND STATE COOPERATIVE FEDERATIONS
summary: In a written Rajya Sabha reply, Union Home and Cooperation Minister Amit Shah explained how National Cooperative Organics Limited (NCOL) coordinates with State Cooperative Federations on organic farming, procurement, processing, branding and marketing. NCOL signs MoUs with State Cooperative Departments/Nodal Agencies, involves State Cooperative Federations, PACS, FPOs and other cooperative institutions as members/partners in the organic value chain under the 'Bharat Organics' brand, and facilitates formation of NPOP-certified Internal Control System (ICS) groups through cooperatives.

title: Safety Fencing Along 19,700 km of Railway Tracks to Prevent Trespassing and Ensure Safe Train Operations
summary: Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw informed the Lok Sabha that about 19,700 km of safety fencing has been installed along railway tracks across India, including in Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh, to prevent trespassing and ensure safe train operations. The Railways is also taking legal action against those involved in stone pelting on trains and running awareness programmes like OPERATION SATHI to sensitize communities living near tracks. Preventive measures include vigilance drives, sensitized train escorting parties, coordination with GRP/local police, and State Level Security Committees chaired by state DGPs.

title: Central Government Strengthens Access to Higher Education for SC Students through POST-MATRIC SCHOLARSHIP SCHEME
summary: The Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment informed the Rajya Sabha that the Post-Matric Scholarship (PMS) Scheme for Scheduled Caste students aims to raise the Gross Enrollment Ratio of SC students in higher education, targeting those from the poorest households with a family income ceiling of ₹2.5 lakh per annum. The scheme is open-ended, demand-driven, and implemented via States/UTs, with Central share released after verification of data on the National Scholarship Portal. Chhattisgarh received a total of ₹203.70 crore in Central Assistance between 2021-22 and 2025-26, benefiting 4,47,482 students, with annual disbursements ranging from ₹29 crore to ₹53.60 crore.

title: RailOne App Reaches 4.76 Crore Downloads, Records 10 Lakh Daily Average Ticket Bookings
summary: The Ministry of Railways informed the Lok Sabha that the RailOne App, launched on 01.07.2025 to integrate reserved, unreserved and platform ticketing along with train enquiry, PNR status and RailMadad, has crossed 4.76 crore downloads and now averages 10 lakh ticket bookings daily (2.79 lakh reserved and 7.24 lakh unreserved) as of 02.08.2026. The release also highlighted the National Train Enquiry System (NTES), which handles over 6 crore enquiries daily and up to 80,000 concurrent users, reducing crowding at railway enquiry counters. Currently about 89% of reserved tickets are booked online (up from 49% in 2013-14), and nearly 39% of unreserved tickets are booked via non-counter modes.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Government Policies and Interventions

title: Allocation Stands At ₹705.11 Crore In 2023-24, ₹539.44 Crore In 2024-25 And ₹557.42 Crore In 2025-26, Amounting To A Total Allocation Of ₹1,801.97 Crores Over The Three-Year Period Under WELFARE SCHEMES FOR SENIOR CITIZENS
summary: In a Rajya Sabha written reply, the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment stated that no scholarship applications or dues are pending under SHREYAS-SC, and that there has been no reduction in de-addiction centre funding over the last three years. It also disclosed budget allocations for welfare schemes for senior citizens: ₹705.11 crore (2023-24), ₹539.44 crore (2024-25), and ₹557.42 crore (2025-26), totaling ₹1,801.97 crore. The reply also detailed the structure of scholarship schemes for SCs, OBCs (PM-YASASVI), and persons with disabilities.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Government Policies and Interventions

title: Parliament Question: Vacancies in Universities
summary: In a Rajya Sabha written reply, the Minister of State for Education informed Parliament about the framework for filling faculty vacancies in Central Higher Education Institutions (CHEIs), noting that recruitment is done autonomously by respective institutions while state university vacancies are not centrally tracked. The reply detailed Mission Mode recruitment drives since 2021, under which 32,114 posts, including 18,757 faculty positions, have been filled up to 23 May 2026. It also referenced quality initiatives like UGC's CU-CHAYAN portal and the Malaviya Mission Teacher Training Program (MMTTP).
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Government Policies and Interventions

title: PREPARATORY ACTIVITIES FOR CENSUS 2027
summary: The Ministry of Home Affairs informed the Rajya Sabha that the first phase of Census 2027 (Houselisting and Housing Census) has been completed in 31 States/UTs, with the remaining states expected to finish by September 2026. The second phase (Population Enumeration) for Ladakh and snow-bound areas of J&K, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand will run from 1-30 September 2026, with a revisional round from 1-5 October 2026 and a self-enumeration option from 17-31 August 2026. The Ministry has deployed digital tools including the Census Management and Monitoring System (CMMS) Portal and an online self-enumeration facility, and has released ₹4102 crore to States/UTs for training, manpower, infrastructure and honorarium payments.

title: DRUG TRAFFICKING CASES
summary: The Ministry of Home Affairs outlined India's multi-pronged strategy against cross-border smuggling and drug trafficking, including advanced surveillance, border infrastructure, and intelligence coordination. It highlighted the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan's expansion to all districts, reaching over 29 crore people since 2020, and detailed the Vision Document on Narcotics Control (2026-2029), the NCORD coordination mechanism, and NDPS Act seizure data from NCRB for 2022-2024.

title: Parliament Question: Regulations of Education Fees
summary: In a written Rajya Sabha reply on 12 August 2026, Minister of State for Education Jayant Chaudhary clarified that regulation of fees charged by private schools and colleges falls under State Governments/UTs since education is on the Concurrent List and schools not owned by the Centre are state-regulated. He noted that the RTE Act, 2009 mandates 25% reservation for weaker sections in private unaided schools and bans capitation fees, while CBSE bye-laws require School Management Committee approval for fee revisions and prohibit forcing purchases from specific vendors. Deemed universities are governed by UGC's 2023 Regulations on fee structures, and private universities follow their respective state Acts.

title: AI-ENABLED CYBER CRIME PREVENTION AND DIGITAL IDENTITY PROTECTION
summary: In a written reply to the Rajya Sabha, MoS Home Affairs Bandi Sanjay Kumar detailed the Central Government's multi-pronged strategy to combat cybercrime, including AI-enabled crime, through the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C). Key initiatives include the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal, the '1930' helpline, the Suspect Registry, Samanvaya and Pratibimb platforms, Cyber Commandos, and CERT-In's threat monitoring systems. The reply cited data such as over Rs. 11,158 crore saved via the Citizen Financial Cyber Fraud Reporting and Management System and over 29,837 arrests facilitated through the Pratibimb module, up to 30 June 2026.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Government Policies and Interventions
GS Paper 3 - Awareness in IT and Emerging Technologies

title: Parliament Question: Availability of Special Educators in Schools
summary: In a Rajya Sabha written reply on 12 August 2026, the Ministry of Education stated that recruitment of teachers, including Special Educators, is a state subject, with the Centre supporting inclusive education through Samagra Shiksha and PM SHRI schemes. As per UDISE+ 2025-26 data, 22.11 lakh Children with Special Needs (CwSN) are enrolled nationally, but only about 1.17 lakh schools (of many more) have a dedicated Special Educator. The Department has notified a Pupil-Teacher Ratio for Special Educators (1:10 at primary, 1:15 at upper-primary level) and supports teacher capacity-building via NCERT, NCTE, CBSE and the Rehabilitation Council of India (RCI).
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Government Policies and Interventions

title: Parliament Question: Mother Tongue Based AI Learning System for Tribal and Multilingual Area
summary: In a written Rajya Sabha reply on 12 August 2026, MoS Education Dr Sukanta Majumdar detailed government initiatives using AI/ML for promoting Indian languages, including tribal languages like Santhali and Mundari, in line with NEP 2020's multilingualism goals. Key initiatives cited include the BharatGen multimodal LLM project (anchored at IIT Bombay), AI translation tools ANUVADINI and BHASHINI, and the Central Institute of Indian Languages' (CIIL) work on tribal language primers, datasets and a Santhali course on SWAYAM. BHASHINI hosts over 360 AI language models, 22+ language services, and a corpus of 246 million parallel sentence pairs, while CIIL's LDC-IL project has built speech and text datasets for Santhali and Mundari.

title: PRAHAAR
summary: The Ministry of Home Affairs informed the Rajya Sabha that it launched 'PRAHAAR', India's first comprehensive National Counter Terrorism Policy & Strategy, on 23 February 2026. Built on seven pillars, it adopts a 'whole of government' and 'whole of society' approach covering prevention, proportionate response, capacity aggregation, rule-of-law compliance, counter-radicalization, international alignment, and resilience. It strengthens real-time intelligence sharing via the Multi Agency Centre (MAC), coordinates State police with central forces like the NSG, targets terror financing including crypto wallets and dark web activity, and aligns with FATF standards. The NIA also organizes an Annual Anti-Terror Conference (ATC) to review and refine the strategy.

title: NDMA'S NATIONAL PREPAREDNESS FRAMEWORK FOR BIOLOGICAL BIOSECURITY THREATS
summary: In a written Rajya Sabha reply, MoS Home Affairs Nityanand Rai stated that India has an institutional framework to respond to biological disasters, anchored in the NDMA Guidelines on Management of Biological Disasters (2008) and the National Disaster Management Plan (2019). Key measures include disease surveillance under IDSP, a network of 150+ ICMR Viral Research and Diagnostic Laboratories (VRDLs), two mobile BSL-3 labs, PM-ABHIM for health infrastructure strengthening, and CBRN-trained NDRF battalions that conduct multi-agency mock drills with states, CAPFs, and health departments.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Government Policies and Interventions

title: PARLIAMENT QUESTIONS: Access to Higher Education under National Digital University Initiative
summary: In a written Rajya Sabha reply on 12 August 2026, Minister of State for Education Dr Sukanta Majumdar detailed progress under the National Digital University Initiative, aligned with NEP 2020. The NIELIT Digital University (NDU) Platform, launched in October 2025 by MeitY's NIELIT, has reached learners in over 750 districts with more than 2.70 lakh registrations and offers 100+ courses in emerging tech areas. Additionally, the SWAYAM Plus platform under the NMEICT scheme offers 500+ employability-focused courses curated from 80+ industry partners across 15 sectors, with over 6 lakh enrollments.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Issues relating to Human Resource Development

title: CYBER FRAUDSTERS EMPTYING BANK ACCOUNTS BY SENDING FAKE E-CHALLANS
summary: In a written Rajya Sabha reply, MHA Minister of State Bandi Sanjay Kumar addressed cyber fraud via fake e-challans, noting NCRB does not maintain specific data on such cases. He detailed government mechanisms to combat cybercrime, including CFCFRMS (which saved over Rs.11,158 crore across 32.80 lakh complaints till 30.06.2026), the Sahyog Portal (blocking 2,77,053+ fraudulent digital assets), CyTrain training portal, the Cyber Commando programme, and National-Digital Investigation Support Centres for forensic assistance.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Centre-State Relations: Seventh Schedule

title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: UGC Funding and Institutional Autonomy
summary: In a written Rajya Sabha reply, the Ministry of Education gave year-wise data (2021-22 to 2025-26) on UGC fund releases and expenditure, funds channelled to Central Universities and Deemed Universities, and Central Share released to States/UTs under RUSA/PM-USHA. It also noted that UGC no longer gives development grants to State Universities post-RUSA implementation, referenced the UGC 2018 teacher-qualification Regulations, and confirmed that the Viksit Bharat Shiksha Adhisthan Bill, 2025, introduced in Lok Sabha on 15 December 2025, has been referred to a Joint Parliamentary Committee.

title: VIBRANT VILLAGES PROGRAMME–II
summary: The Ministry of Home Affairs informed the Rajya Sabha that Vibrant Villages Programme-I (VVP-I), approved in February 2023, covers 46 blocks along the northern border in five States/UTs, with 2,906 projects sanctioned and ₹959.66 crore released so far. Vibrant Villages Programme-II (VVP-II), approved in April 2025 as a Central Sector Scheme with a ₹6,839 crore outlay till FY2028-29, extends coverage to 1,954 villages in 334 blocks along other International Land Borders across 17 States/UTs. A High-Powered Committee chaired by the Cabinet Secretary has been constituted to relax scheme guidelines of various ministries for effective implementation in these border villages.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Government Policies and Interventions

title: Over 50,000 Saplings Planted Across 31 States on Hariyali Amavasya Under Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan’s Green Initiative
summary: On the occasion of Hariyali Amavasya, over 50,000 saplings were planted across 31 states in a nationwide drive led by Union Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan in collaboration with the 'Vriksh Mitra Parivar', drawing on PM Modi's 'Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam' initiative. The main event was held at PBG Ground, Central Ridge, near Talkatora Stadium, New Delhi, with participation from ministers, MPs, officials, farmers and citizens, alongside parallel plantation drives in villages, towns, panchayats and institutions nationwide. Chouhan urged citizens to plant at least one tree annually, mark personal milestones as 'Vriksh Parv', and emphasised environmental care alongside agricultural sustainability, referencing Mission LiFE and plastic reduction. Delhi ministers Manjinder Singh Sirsa and Parvesh Verma highlighted Delhi's participation and the need to balance development with environmental protection.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 3 - Environment and Ecology: Conservation
GS Paper 2 - Government Policies and Interventions

title: Over 50,000 Saplings Planted Across 31 States on Hariyali Amavasya Under Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan’s Green Initiative
summary: On Hariyali Amavasya (12 August 2026), Union Agriculture & Rural Development Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan led a nationwide tree plantation drive with the 'Vriksh Mitra Parivar', under which more than 50,000 saplings were planted across 31 states. The main event was held at PBG Ground, Central Ridge, near Talkatora Stadium, New Delhi, drawing momentum from PM Modi's 'Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam' initiative. Chouhan urged citizens to plant at least one tree annually, protect existing plantations, and adopt Mission LiFE practices, while Delhi ministers Manjinder Singh Sirsa and Parvesh Verma highlighted complementary state-level efforts and the need to balance development with environmental protection.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Government Policies and Interventions
GS Paper 3 - Climate Change: India's mitigation initiatives (Mission LiFE, NDC targets)

title: Indian Railways Approves Provision of Kavach Version 4.0 on 660 Route Km of Izzatnagar Division of North Eastern Railway at ₹295 crore
summary: Indian Railways has sanctioned installation of Kavach Version 4.0, the indigenous Automatic Train Protection system, across 660 route km of the Izzatnagar Division of North Eastern Railway at an estimated cost of ₹295 crore. The work falls under the broader project of equipping balance sections of Indian Railways with Kavach along with an LTE-based communication backbone. Kavach aims to prevent Signal Passed at Danger incidents and train collisions by continuously monitoring train movement and automatically applying brakes when needed.

title: Indian Railways Approves Construction of 4 Lane ROB at Geratpur-Ahmedabad Section in Gujarat at ₹153 Crore
summary: Indian Railways has sanctioned construction of a 4-lane Road Over Bridge (ROB) at Level Crossing No. 305 on the Geratpur-Ahmedabad section of Western Railway in Gujarat, at a cost of ₹153 crore. The bridge will have a 106-metre railway bridge portion with two 53-metre composite girders, a 150-metre viaduct, and a 595-metre road approach, aimed at eliminating the level crossing and enabling uninterrupted vehicular movement.

title: Financial Inclusion in India: Banking Every Citizen, Empowering Every Household
summary: This PIB backgrounder consolidates a decade of progress in India's financial inclusion drive, citing the RBI's Financial Inclusion Index rising from 43.4 (March 2017) to 70.0 (March 2026) and the World Bank's Global Findex 2025 showing 89% account ownership among Indian adults. It details the banking access network (1.81 lakh branches, 99.92% villages covered within 5 km, IPPB and Business Correspondent networks), flagship schemes (PMJDY, JAM Trinity, DBT, PMJJBY, PMSBY, APY, Mudra, PM SVANidhi, KCC, Jan Samarth), UPI's explosive growth, and financial literacy initiatives (NCFE, FEPA) alongside a 2025 Nationwide Financial Inclusion Saturation Campaign.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Government Policies and Interventions/Welfare Schemes
GS Paper 2 - Social Security and Vulnerable Sections

title: HIGHWAY INFRASTRUCTURE FINANCING AND INVESTMENT
summary: The Ministry of Road Transport & Highways has outlined its strategy to boost highway infrastructure financing by prioritizing access-controlled expressways, ring roads/bypasses for cities above one lakh population, coastal roads, and connectivity to ports, airports and industrial nodes. To attract private investment, it has reformed Model Concession Agreements, Toll Operate and Transfer (TOT) contracts, introduced Public InvIT, and amended BOT bidding/concession documents covering eligibility, dispute resolution, and compensation provisions. This was stated by Union Minister Nitin Gadkari in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha on 12 August 2026.

title: IMPLEMENTATION STATUS OF PM RAHAT SCHEME
summary: The Ministry of Road Transport & Highways informed Rajya Sabha about the implementation status of the PM-RAHAT scheme, launched nationwide on 13.02.2026 under Section 162 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, to provide cashless treatment up to Rs.1.5 lakh per road accident victim for 7 days. As of 31.07.2026, 22,481 victims across 34 States/UTs had benefitted, with SHAs approving claims worth Rs.12.59 crore and Rs.10.56 crore already disbursed to hospitals. Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh recorded the highest number of cases.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Government Policies and Interventions

title: “One Herb, One Standard” to Strengthen Quality and Credibility of Traditional Medicines: Union Minister Shri Prataprao Jadhav
summary: The Pharmacopoeia Commission for Indian Medicine & Homoeopathy (PCIM&H) under the Ministry of Ayush and the Indian Pharmacopoeia Commission (IPC) under the Ministry of Health & Family Welfare renewed their MoU for a further three years to implement the 'One Herb, One Standard' initiative. This inter-ministerial effort aims to develop harmonised, scientifically robust quality standards for single plant-origin drugs used across Ayurveda, Siddha, Sowa-Rigpa, Unani and Homoeopathy. The renewed phase builds on 50 monographs developed since the original 2022 MoU and will factor in both Indian and international quality benchmarks.

title: Ministry of Women and Child Development has issued National Minimum Standards and Protocol in 2024 for setting up creches

ministry.name: Ministry of Women and Child Development

summary: The Ministry of Women and Child Development informed the Rajya Sabha that it issued National Minimum Standards and Protocol in 2024 for setting up creches, mandating compliance with child protection and safety rules. This is linked to the Anganwadi cum Creches (Palna) scheme, launched from 1 April 2022, which currently has 4,172 operational Anganwadi-cum-Crèche Centres (AWCCs) across the country. The Code on Social Security, 2020 (effective 21.11.2025) has subsumed the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961, with Section 67 mandating creche facilities in establishments with 50 or more employees.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Government Policies and Interventions

title: Government remains committed to ensuring that children are able to benefit from digital technologies while being protected from online harms

ministry.name: Ministry of Women and Child Development

summary: In a Rajya Sabha reply, the Ministry of Women and Child Development outlined the government's multi-pronged framework to protect children online while enabling digital access to education and services. This includes the IT Act 2000, IT Intermediary Guidelines 2021, the Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023, I4C's cybercrime reporting portal, and NCPCR initiatives like 'Being Safe Online' guidelines and a 2021 study on mobile/internet effects on children covering 5,811 respondents across six states. Education Ministry bodies (CBSE, NCERT) have also integrated cyber safety into curricula and teacher training.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Statutory and Regulatory Bodies

title: Ministry of Women and Child Development is implementing Centrally Sponsored Schemes in the country for the welfare of women and children

ministry.name: Ministry of Women and Child Development

summary: The Ministry of Women and Child Development informed Rajya Sabha about its Centrally Sponsored Schemes under three verticals — Mission Shakti (women's safety and empowerment), Saksham Anganwadi & Poshan 2.0 (nutrition), and Mission Vatsalya (child protection). The release details Mission Shakti's sub-schemes such as One Stop Centres, Women Helpline (181), Beti Bachao Beti Padhao, Shakti Sadan, Sakhi Niwas, Palna, PMMVY and SANKALP: HEW, giving nationwide and Odisha-specific beneficiary data up to mid-2026. It also explains the funding mechanism via State/UT governments under PFMS and annual review by the Programme Approval Board.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Government Policies and Interventions
GS Paper 2 - Centre-State financial relations and Centrally Sponsored Schemes

title: Government accords highest priority for ensuring safety and security of children and has undertaken various initiatives in this regard

ministry.name: Ministry of Women and Child Development

summary: In a Rajya Sabha reply, the Ministry of Women and Child Development outlined measures for child protection, centered on the POCSO Act, 2012 (amended in 2019 to add death penalty provisions) and POCSO Rules, 2020. It highlighted the role of 'Support Persons' who assist child victims during investigation and trial, NCPCR's Model Guidelines for their selection, and the POCSO Tracking Portal for real-time case monitoring. Implementation responsibility rests with States/UTs, with the Ministry providing advisories and capacity-building support.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Government Policies and Interventions
GS Paper 2 - Statutory and Regulatory Bodies

title: Ministry introduced Anganwadi cum Creches under Palna for providing day care creche facilities in safe and secure environment to children

ministry.name: Ministry of Women and Child Development

summary: The Ministry of Women and Child Development informed the Rajya Sabha that Anganwadi-cum-Crèches (AWCCs) under the Palna Scheme, launched from 1 April 2022, currently number 4,172 operational units across India, providing day-care facilities for children aged 6 months to 6 years regardless of their mothers' employment status. Palna is a centrally sponsored scheme under the Samarthya vertical of Mission Shakti, funded on a 60:40 Centre-State basis (90:10 for NE/special category states, 100% for UTs without legislature). The reply also noted that the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961 has been subsumed under the Code on Social Security, 2020 (effective 21.11.2025), whose Section 67 mandates creche facilities for establishments with 50 or more employees.

title: PRESS RELEASE OF CONSUMER PRICE INDEX ON BASE 2024=100 FOR JULY, 2026
summary: MoSPI's provisional CPI data (Base 2024=100) shows all-India retail inflation at 4.45% in July 2026, up from 4.38% in June 2026, with rural inflation (4.84%) higher than urban (3.96%). Food inflation (CFPI) rose to 5.52%, driven by sharp spikes in silver jewellery (109.84%), ginger (83.62%), garlic (35.36%) and gold/diamond jewellery (32.98%), while potato, motor vehicles, lady's finger, peas and tomato prices fell year-on-year. Telangana (6.32%) and Andhra Pradesh (5.72%) recorded the highest state-level inflation among major states, and housing inflation stood at a relatively low 2.22%. Data was collected from 1,407 urban and 1,465 rural markets with a 100% response rate; the August 2026 release is due on 14 September 2026.

title: Compounded annual growth rate of Manufacturing GVA at constant prices (2022-23 base) as per revised series during 2022-23 to 2025-26 is 10.88%
summary: MoSPI data presented in Lok Sabha shows that as per the revised National Accounts Statistics series (2022-23 base), the Manufacturing sector's share in total GVA stayed nearly stable at 14.5-14.8% between 2022-23 and 2025-26. Manufacturing GVA at constant prices grew 12.7%, 9.3%, and 10.7% in 2023-24, 2024-25 (FRE), and 2025-26 (PE) respectively, giving a CAGR of 10.88% over the period. The government cited multiple structural reforms like PLI schemes, PM GatiShakti, and NICDP as measures to strengthen manufacturing resilience.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Government Policies and Interventions

title: AI uncovers hidden cancer stem cells responsible for tumour recurrence paving way to precision medicine
summary: Researchers at S. N. Bose National Centre for Basic Sciences (SNBNCBS), an autonomous institute under the Department of Science and Technology, in collaboration with Ashoka University, have developed an AI framework called ACSCeND that identifies three distinct developmental states of cancer stem-like cells (pluripotent-like, multipotent-like, unipotent-like) from tumour gene-expression data. The tool, led by Dr. Shubhasis Haldar, builds on the team's earlier OncoMark platform and was validated across more than 25,000 tumour samples from databases like TCGA and PRECOG, showing that tumours rich in pluripotent-like cancer stem cells are linked to poorer survival, higher recurrence, and reduced response to immunotherapy. The framework combines single-cell sequencing knowledge with deep learning to analyse widely available bulk RNA sequencing data, making advanced stem-cell profiling accessible even where single-cell experiments are unavailable.

title: Skill Development Programmes

ministry.name: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship

summary: The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) provided a status update on skilling initiatives under the Skill India Mission (SIM), covering schemes like PMKVY, Jan Shikshan Sansthan (JSS), National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS) and Craftsman Training Scheme (CTS) via ITIs, with state/UT-wise data for 2021-22 to 2025-26. It highlighted that 26,385 candidates were reported placed in Kerala under PMKVY 1.0-3.0, and detailed quality and industry-alignment measures such as NCVET regulation, Skill India Digital Hub (SIDH), Indian Institutes of Skills (IIS), Sector Skill Councils, the Apprenticeship Embedded Degree Programme (AEDP), and the newly launched PM-SETU scheme (Rs. 60,000 crore) to upgrade 1,000 government ITIs in a hub-and-spoke model.

title: Impact of AI and Emerging Technologies

ministry.name: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship

summary: In a written Rajya Sabha reply, MSDE Minister Jayant Chaudhary detailed the government's efforts to align skill development programmes with AI and emerging technologies. Key measures include 36 Sector Skill Councils, PMKVY courses aligned with Industry 4.0, DGT's new-age courses in 5G/AI/Cybersecurity, the SOAR initiative for school students, FutureSkills Prime platform, NCVET's qualification framework, PM SETU for upgrading 1,000 ITIs, and the Apprenticeship Embedded Degree Programme under NEP 2020.

title: Skill Development Under PMKVY

ministry.name: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship

summary: In a Rajya Sabha written reply, the Minister of State for Skill Development and Entrepreneurship stated that under PMKVY 4.0, over 600 courses have been introduced in future-oriented sectors like AI, Drone Technology, 5G, Solar Energy, 3D Printing, Semiconductors and IoT, training more than 5.44 lakh candidates by 30 June 2026. ₹414.86 crore has been utilized for training in these new-age job roles, with industry bodies like NCVET, 36 Sector Skill Councils, and recognised Awarding Bodies (HCL, IBM, Bajaj Finserv, Microsoft) ensuring industry-aligned curricula. The scheme mandates On-the-Job Training and has set up the Kaushal Samiksha Kendra for monitoring quality and detecting irregularities via biometric attendance verification.

title: Outcome-Based Funding For Skills Training Centres

ministry.name: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship

summary: The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) and NSDC have launched the Skills Outcomes Fund (SOF), a blended-finance mechanism with a Rs.530 crore corpus (Rs.225 crore from the Ministry, Rs.305 crore from CSR/philanthropic sources). SOF pays training providers only upon verified achievement of milestones - Certification (30%), Job Placement (40%), and 3-Month Retention (30%) - rather than for enrolment, and prioritises women and low-income youth. The information was shared by MoS Jayant Chaudhary in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha on 12 August 2026.

title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE, RESEARCH AND INNOVATION
summary: In a written Lok Sabha reply on 12 August 2026, the Ministry of Science & Technology detailed India's major schemes promoting emerging technologies, including the RDI Fund (Rs 1 lakh crore), National Quantum Mission (Rs 6,003.65 crore), NM-ICPS (Rs 3,660 crore), Bio-RIDE (Rs 9,197 crore), India AI Mission (Rs 10,371.92 crore) and India Semiconductor Mission (Rs 76,000 crore). It also reported that Gross Expenditure on R&D (GERD) as a percentage of GDP rose from 0.64% in 2020-21 to 0.84% in 2023-24, with absolute GERD tripling from Rs 79,355.89 crore (2013-14) to Rs 2,44,767.81 crore (2023-24). The reply listed 25 Technology Innovation Hubs under NM-ICPS and 4 Technology Hubs under the National Quantum Mission across various IITs and institutions, along with fellowship and infrastructure schemes supporting researchers.

title: Integration of Artificial Intelligence Into The Skill Development Ecosystem

ministry.name: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship

summary: The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship informed the Rajya Sabha about steps to integrate Artificial Intelligence into India's skilling ecosystem, including the Skill India Digital Hub (SIDH), the SOAR programme, PMKVY 4.0, NAPS, ITI upgradation via AI courses, and the PM-SETU scheme. As of August 2026, over 5.17 lakh learners enrolled and 1.006 lakh certified under SOAR, while PMKVY 4.0 has trained 5.44 lakh and certified 3.73 lakh candidates in future-skills roles. State-wise data show Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Telangana and Uttar Pradesh leading in AI-related training and certification.

title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: BENEFICIARIES SELECTED UNDER INSPIRE SHE
summary: In a written Lok Sabha reply, the Minister of State for Science & Technology Dr. Jitendra Singh provided year-wise and state-wise data on the INSPIRE-SHE scholarship scheme from 2019-20 to 2024-25, confirming the annual scholarship targets have been met. The data shows applications, selections, fund utilisation (ranging from about Rs.212-238 crore annually), and gender/rural-urban breakdowns of beneficiaries, with female beneficiaries outnumbering males since 2021-22 and rural students consistently forming the majority of selections.

title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: RURAL TECHNOLOGY DEMONSTRATION PROJECTS
summary: In response to a Parliament question, the Ministry of Science & Technology detailed how the Department of Science and Technology (DST) and Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR) have implemented technology demonstration projects for rural livelihoods, including in the Khajuraho Lok Sabha region of Madhya Pradesh. Key highlights include a new SC/ST Cell established in March 2026 at the Madhya Pradesh Council of Science & Technology covering 20 districts, and CSIR's Aroma Mission activities in Bundelkhand where nearly 1,000 farmers adopted aromatic crop cultivation across Panna and Chhatarpur districts using Field Distillation Units. The release also lists DST schemes such as STI Hub, Women Technology Parks (WTP), SUNIL, and NM-ICPS, along with technology transfer initiatives by autonomous institutions like ARI Pune, JNCASR Bengaluru, IASST Guwahati, NIF Ahmedabad, and NECTAR Shillong.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Government Policies and Interventions

title: Industry Relevant Skill Training

ministry.name: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship

summary: The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship informed the Rajya Sabha about the National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS), launched in 2016 and continuing as NAPS-2 since 2022-23, which promotes industry-aligned apprenticeship training via the Apprentices Act, 1961. The government provides stipend support (25% of establishment's stipend, capped at ₹1,500/month) via Direct Benefit Transfer, with ₹1,573.46 crore disbursed across states from 2023-24 to 2026-27. The release also highlights measures like NCVET regulation, Sector Skill Councils, Industry 4.0-aligned courses, and a rise in women apprentices from 7.74% (2016-17) to 24.95% (2025-26).

title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: NATIONAL MISSION ON INTERDISCIPLINARY CYBER-PHYSICAL SYSTEMS (NM-ICPS)
summary: The Department of Science and Technology's National Mission on Interdisciplinary Cyber-Physical Systems (NM-ICPS), launched in 2018 with a Rs 3660 crore outlay over nine years, has established 25 Technology Innovation Hubs (TIHs) across premier institutions to develop technologies like AI, IoT, robotics, cybersecurity and quantum systems. In 2025-26, four top-performing TIHs were upgraded to Technology Translation Research Parks (TTRPs) at IIT Kanpur, IISc Bengaluru, IIT (ISM) Dhanbad and IIT Indore. The Mission has produced over 1100 technologies, 1300 technology products and incubated more than 1130 start-ups, including notable outputs like BharatGen's multilingual AI models and 5G-Advanced radio units. This was disclosed by Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh in a written Lok Sabha reply.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Government Policies and Interventions

title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: CAREER PROGRESSION FOR WOMEN RESEARCHERS
summary: In a written Lok Sabha reply, the Minister of State for Science & Technology, Dr. Jitendra Singh, cited data showing women's participation in STEM research careers rose from 13% in 2000-01 to 18.6% in 2020-21 and 29% in 2023-24. He detailed studies identifying barriers to women's career progression and outlined government schemes like WISE-KIRAN, BioCARe, and the Women Scientist Scheme that support women researchers returning after career breaks. Under WISE-KIRAN, over 4,000 women scientists have been supported and 942 trained in IPR, while BioCARe has supported 415 women researchers.

title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: INNOVATION IN SCIENCE PURSUIT FOR INSPIRED RESEARCH (INSPIRE) PROGRAMME
summary: In a written Lok Sabha reply, the Minister of State for Science & Technology Dr. Jitendra Singh detailed the INSPIRE programme's four components - MANAK, SHE, Fellowship, and Faculty Fellowship - which support students and researchers from school level to postdoctoral research. Data for 2021-22 to 2025-26 showed INSPIRE-MANAK supporting around 43,000-53,000 students annually, SHE scholarships rising from 18,039 to 24,276, PhD Fellowships around 2,400-3,400, and Faculty Fellowships between 225-477 annually. The reply also outlined outreach efforts targeting rural, remote and aspirational districts through awareness campaigns, exhibitions, and mentorship with IITs, NITs and IISERs.

title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: NATIONAL QUANTUM MISSION
summary: In a written Lok Sabha reply, the Science & Technology Minister detailed progress under the National Quantum Mission (NQM) during 2025-26, including operationalization of four Thematic Hubs with 14 Technical Groups and 17 Project Teams, establishment of research infrastructure at IISc Bengaluru, IIT Bombay, IIT Kanpur and IIT Delhi, capacity-building programmes with AICTE, 23 Quantum Teaching Laboratories, and support to 17 quantum startups. The reply also outlined contributions from DRDO (indigenous QRNGs and RCQCP technology transferred to industry), MeitY's Qniverse quantum computing platform, and ISRO's structured review mechanisms and quantum-ready infrastructure for space applications.

title: Dr. Jitendra Singh Presents Government’s Roadmap for a Self-Reliant and Globally Competitive Nuclear Energy Ecosystem in Lok Sabha
summary: In a written Lok Sabha reply, Dr. Jitendra Singh outlined India's roadmap for nuclear energy self-reliance, targeting 100 GWe nuclear capacity by 2047 under the Nuclear Energy Mission announced in Union Budget 2025-26. Key measures include developing at least five indigenous Small Modular Reactors (SMRs) by 2033, advancing the three-stage nuclear programme for thorium utilisation, and enacting the SHANTI Act, 2025 to enable private sector participation in nuclear manufacturing and R&D.

title: Digital Transformation Strengthens Livestock and Fisheries Sectors

ministry.name: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying

summary: The Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying highlighted digital initiatives strengthening these sectors: the Bharat Pashudhan Portal has registered 39.23 crore livestock under a 12-digit 'Pashu Aadhaar' unique ID system, while the National Fisheries Digital Platform (NFDP) has registered 35.85 lakh fishers and stakeholders. Under Bharat Pashudhan, 17.27 crore artificial inseminations have been recorded benefiting 5.98 crore farmers. The NFDP, launched under PM-MKSSY (a ₹6,000 crore Central Sector Sub-scheme under PMMSY, FY2023-24 to FY2026-27), facilitates credit access, aquaculture insurance incentives, and traceability, though Kisan Credit Card applications are still processed only through banks' own systems.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Government Policies and Interventions

title: Modernization of Dairy Sector and Growth in Milk Production

ministry.name: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying

summary: The Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying informed Parliament about progress under the National Programme for Dairy Development (NPDD) and the Animal Husbandry Infrastructure Development Fund (AHIDF), which support modernization of dairy infrastructure across India. As of June 2026, over 71,000 Dairy Cooperative Societies have been organised or strengthened, 168 LLPD of milk chilling capacity created, and AHIDF-approved projects add 418 LLPD of processing capacity. Milk production rose from 209.96 million metric tonnes in 2020-21 to 247.87 million metric tonnes in 2024-25, with per capita availability increasing from 427 to 485 grams/day.

title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: THIRD-PARTY SECURITY AUDITS OF NUCLEAR POWER PLANTS
summary: In a written Lok Sabha reply, Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh stated that Indian nuclear power plants, including Kudankulam, have robust security measures including periodic AERB and external agency audits, electronic surveillance systems, and cybersecurity protocols coordinated with CERT-In. Emergency Preparedness Plans are regularly tested through Table Top, ICCR, and Mock exercises, with recent ICCR exercises conducted at Kudankulam (April 2025) and Kalpakkam (July 2026, involving the PFBR).

title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: ENVIRONMENTAL SAFEGUARDS FOR HEAVY MINERAL SAND MINING AND RARE EARTH MINERALS
summary: The Atomic Minerals Directorate for Exploration and Research (AMD) has identified a new Beach Sand Minerals deposit named 'Pudupuram-Cuddalore BSM deposit' in Cuddalore district, Tamil Nadu, containing 1.912 million tonnes of Total Heavy Minerals, including monazite, ilmenite and zircon. In a Lok Sabha written reply, the Minister of State detailed government measures to curb illegal beach sand mining and unauthorized monazite exports, including a 2019 notification bringing monazite-bearing BSM deposits under complete government control, canalization of BSM exports through IREL, satellite-based Mining Surveillance System, and mandatory Environmental Impact Assessment and BARC radiological clearance before mining leases in coastal areas.

title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: APPLICATION OF RADIATION TECHNOLOGIES FOR AGRICULTURE AND FOOD SECURITY
summary: In a written Lok Sabha reply, Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh stated that BARC (under the Department of Atomic Energy) has developed 72 improved crop varieties through radiation-induced mutagenesis and cross-breeding, notified for commercial cultivation in collaboration with ICAR and State Agricultural Universities. These include varieties in groundnut, rice, mungbean, mustard, urdbean, pigeonpea and other crops with traits like higher yield, early maturity and climate resilience. DAE also promotes seed distribution, farmer outreach, and radiation-based food preservation technologies, with incentives for food irradiation units under PMKSY, including three such facilities commissioned in Uttar Pradesh.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Government Policies and Interventions

title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: DOMESTIC SELF-SUFFICIENCY IN CRITICAL MEDICAL RADIOISOTOPE SUPPLY
summary: In a written Lok Sabha reply, the Department of Atomic Energy detailed India's production and import of three key medical radioisotopes—Molybdenum-99, Iodine-131, and Lutetium-177—used in nearly 90% of nuclear medicine applications. These are produced at the Dhruva reactor at BARC and supplied via the Board of Radiation & Isotope Technology (BRIT), with BRIT meeting about 90% of confirmed orders under normal conditions, though shortfalls occurred during reactor/facility shutdowns necessitating imports from countries like Russia, Australia, Belgium, Egypt, Poland and South Africa. BARC has now received sanction for a new 'Isotope Production Reactor' project, expected to start production around 2035 with a capacity of 0.5 million Curies, aimed at boosting self-sufficiency.

title: Government Endeavours to Strengthen Credible Information Dissemination through PIB Fact-Checking, Public Service Broadcasting and Digital Media Regulations
summary: In a written Lok Sabha reply, Minister of State Dr. L. Murugan detailed the Government's multi-pronged approach to credible information dissemination: PIB's Fact Check Unit (FCU) counters fake news about government schemes, Doordarshan and Akashvani integrate verified content into their broadcasts, and the IT (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021 regulate digital news and OTT platforms via a three-tier grievance redressal mechanism. The reply also highlighted film sector promotion schemes (DCDFC, India Cine Hub, National Film Heritage Mission) and international media cooperation, including WAVES 2025 in Mumbai and Prasar Bharati's 48 active MoUs with foreign broadcasters.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Role of media, IT rules and digital regulation
GS Paper 2 - Government schemes for social/economic development (film sector)

title: Government Provides ₹10.66 Crore Financial Assistance to 457 Beneficiaries under Dr. Ambedkar Scheme for Inter-Caste Marriages
summary: The Central Government informed the Rajya Sabha that the Dr. Ambedkar Scheme for Social Integration through Inter-Caste Marriages was merged with the Centrally Sponsored Scheme for the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 and SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, effective 31 March 2023, to avoid duplication. Despite the merger, the Dr. Ambedkar Foundation continued processing pending inter-caste marriage cases, releasing ₹10.66 crore to 457 beneficiaries over 2023-24 to 2025-26 (68, 11, and 378 beneficiaries respectively). The information was shared by Minister of State Ramdas Athawale in a written reply.

title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: SPACE STARTUPS
summary: In a written Lok Sabha reply, the Department of Space stated that around 440 space technology startups are registered under DPIIT's Start-up India Portal, with IN-SPACe having granted 113 authorisations to 52 Non-Government Entities including 18 startups. NSIL has signed 118 Technology Transfer Agreements covering 83 ISRO-developed technologies, and cumulative investment in Indian space startups reached about USD 618.5 million as of 31 March 2026. The government listed measures under the Indian Space Policy 2023 including a ₹1,000 crore VC Fund, ₹500 crore Technology Adoption Fund, liberalized FDI policy, and international collaborations spanning over 30 countries, while clarifying there is no current plan for additional space incubation centres in Andhra Pradesh.

title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: PUBLIC-PRIVATE PARTNERSHIP (PPP) MODEL FOR EARTH OBSERVATION SATELLITE CONSTELLATIONS
summary: The Department of Space informed the Lok Sabha that IN-SPACe has formulated a Public-Private Partnership (PPP) framework enabling private industry to design, build, own and operate Earth Observation (EO) satellite constellations end-to-end. Under this framework, IN-SPACe has signed its first commercial EO constellation agreement with a consortium named Allied Orbits Private Limited (led by PixxelSpace India, with Dhruva Space, PierSight Space and Satsure Analytics India), which will build and operate a 12-satellite constellation with optical, hyperspectral and SAR capabilities for over Rs. 1,200 crore, to be operational by 2029. The government has also created financial instruments like the Antariksh Venture Capital Fund, Technology Adoption Fund, and Seed Fund Scheme to support private space investment.

title: Union Minister for Finance & Corporate Affairs Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman delivers keynote address at Seminar on “Role of the New Development Bank in Mobilising Private Capital in Member Countries” in Jaipur, today
summary: Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman delivered the keynote address at a seminar on the role of the New Development Bank (NDB) in mobilising private capital, held on the sidelines of the BRICS Finance Ministers' and Central Bank Governors' Meeting in Jaipur on 12 August 2026. She highlighted India's infrastructure reforms—including VGF, HAM, InvITs, National Infrastructure Pipeline, and PM Gati Shakti—and new Budget 2026-27 initiatives like Dedicated Freight Corridors, High-Speed Rail Corridors, National Waterways, and a Coastal Cargo Promotion Scheme. NDB President Dilma Rousseff also spoke, and the event featured a panel with IRDAI Chairman Ajay Seth, NDB Vice-President Roman Serov, and other BRICS financial and industry leaders.

title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: SPACE VISION 2047
summary: In a written Lok Sabha reply on 12 August 2026, Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh detailed ISRO/Department of Space's 2026 space-based applications for agriculture, disaster management, climate monitoring and developmental programmes like MGNREGA and PMGSY. He also outlined the Space Vision 2047 roadmap covering Earth observation, satellite communication and NavIC-based satellite navigation, including plans for indigenous constellations, 5G/6G integration and lunar PNT services.

title: Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan flags off ‘Har Ghar Tiranga Bike Rally 2026’ dedicated to National Song Vande Mataram, today at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi
summary: On 12 August 2026, Vice-President C. P. Radhakrishnan flagged off the 'Har Ghar Tiranga Bike Rally 2026' from Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, as part of the ongoing Har Ghar Tiranga 2026 campaign dedicated to 150 years of the National Song Vande Mataram. Several Union Cabinet Ministers, Ministers of State and Members of Parliament joined the rally, which also saw participation from over 350 CAPF bikers (including CRPF, BSF, Assam Rifles) and more than 50 special and women biker groups. The Vice-President urged citizens to keep the patriotic spirit alive beyond the rally by actively promoting the Tiranga campaign in their homes, streets and constituencies.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Government Policies and Interventions

title: ATMANIRBHAR PANCHAYAT PROGRAM
summary: The Ministry of Panchayati Raj's Atmanirbhar Panchayat Programme is a four-year initiative to make Panchayats financially self-sufficient by generating Own Source Revenue (OSR) through projects using untapped local assets, selected via a State/National open challenge process. Eligible Gram and Block Panchayats (with minimum tenure and OSR thresholds) receive technical assistance rather than direct funding, with financing facilitated through PPP, CSR, and scheme convergence. As of 4 August 2026, 30 project proposals from 28 Panchayats had been received on the dedicated digital portal. The information was shared by Minister Rajiv Ranjan Singh in a written reply in Rajya Sabha on 12 August 2026.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Government Policies and Interventions

title: RLB GRANTS RECOMMENDED BY SIXTEENTH FINANCE COMMISSION
summary: The Sixteenth Finance Commission (FC-16) has recommended Rs. 4,35,236 crore in grants for Rural Local Bodies (RLBs)/Panchayati Raj Institutions across 28 states for the award period 2026-31, with Rs. 11,664 crore earmarked for Chhattisgarh. The Ministry of Finance issued Operational Guidelines on 21.05.2026 detailing Basic Grant (80%, split into Tied and Untied) and Performance Grant (20%, Untied) components. The Ministry of Panchayati Raj also highlighted multiple initiatives to boost Panchayats' Own Source Revenue and ensure transparent fund utilisation, including SAMARTH Panchayat portal, eGramSwaraj, AuditOnline, and SVAMITVA scheme.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Government Policies and Interventions

title: IMPLEMENTATION OF RASHTRIYA GRAM SWARAJ ABHIYAN (RGSA) IN WEST BENGAL
summary: In a written Rajya Sabha reply on 12 August 2026, Union Minister Rajiv Ranjan Singh (Lalan Singh) detailed the implementation of the Centrally Sponsored Scheme Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan (RGSA) in West Bengal since FY 2022-23. Rs.130.65 crore was released as Central Share over four years, 5,17,632 elected representatives were trained, 199 Panchayat Bhawan units and 1,712 computer units were approved, with 124 Bhawans and 1,185 computers completed so far. The reply also noted progress under the e-Panchayat Mission Mode Project, including GeM onboarding and GPDP uploads on the eGramSwaraj portal.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Indian Polity: Panchayati Raj and 73rd Amendment

title: STRENGTHENING DIGITAL PANCHAYAT GOVERNANCE THROUGH EGRAMSWARAJ
summary: The Ministry of Panchayati Raj informed the Rajya Sabha that its eGramSwaraj platform, under the e-Panchayat Mission Mode Project of the Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan (RGSA), has been integrated with PFMS, GeM, BSNL, BHASHINI and IMD to strengthen digital governance in Panchayati Raj Institutions. In FY 2025-26, 98.65% of Gram Panchayats uploaded their Gram Panchayat Development Plans and 95% made payments worth ₹57,337 crore via the eGramSwaraj-PFMS interface. The Ministry also launched SabhaSaar, an AI voice-to-text tool for summarising Gram Sabha proceedings, which has been used by over 1.35 lakh Gram Panchayats to process more than 3.57 lakh minutes of meetings.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Government Policies and Interventions

title: Reforming India’s Tribunal System
summary: The Tribunals Reforms Bill, 2026, passed by Parliament, establishes a judiciary-led National Tribunals Commission (NTC) to handle appointments, service conditions, performance review and oversight of 16 tribunals, replacing the Central Government's direct role under the Tribunals Reforms Act, 2021, which it repeals. The Bill responds to the Supreme Court's Madras Bar Association judgment (2026), which struck down parts of the 2021 Act and directed creation of an independent commission. The NTC will have a judicial majority, be headed by a former Supreme Court judge or Chief Justice of a High Court, and oversee Search-cum-Selection Committees, a National Tribunals Data Grid, and financial/administrative autonomy for tribunals, with CAG audit and parliamentary oversight.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Separation of Powers and Judicial Independence

title: Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal Calls for Fair Trading Practices and Taking ‘Make in India’ from Local to Global
summary: Union Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal, speaking at the inaugural ceremony of the Bharatiya Vyapar Mahotsav at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, called on Indian businesses to adopt fair trading practices, embrace a circular economy, and take 'Make in India' products from local to global markets. He noted that India has signed nine Free Trade Agreements opening new markets, that goods and services exports reached a record level last year with the target of achieving 1 trillion dollars in exports this fiscal year, and that India aims to become a 30 trillion dollar economy by 2047 from its current size of about 4 trillion dollars.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Government Policies and Interventions

title: Prime Minister Shares glimpses of his address during the release of Autobiography of Former President Shri Ram Nath Kovind Ji
summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi attended and shared reflections on the release of former President Ram Nath Kovind's autobiography, titled 'Triumph of the Indian Republic: My Life, My Struggles'. In posts on X, Modi praised the book for highlighting Kovind's personal struggles and his service as an MP, Governor, and President, calling it an inspiration reflecting the strengths of Indian democracy.

title: National AI Skilling Initiative Records 60,253 Enrolments in Phase I; IICT and Private Sector Partners have Jointly Developed Curriculum to Equip Students with Industry-Relevant AI Skills
summary: In a written Lok Sabha reply, MoS Dr. L. Murugan stated that Phase I of the National AI Skilling Initiative has recorded 60,253 applications/enrolments, with 4,620 participants completing 2 modules and 552 completing all 4 modules. Phase I comprises four modules (33 hours total) across two learning platforms covering AI Essentials, Prompting Essentials, Introduction to Generative AI, and Generative AI Leader. The curriculum was jointly developed by IICT and private sector partners, with Phase II details still under finalisation.

title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: MISSION KARMAYOGI

ministry.name: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions

summary: In a written Lok Sabha reply, Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh provided an update on Mission Karmayogi (National Programme for Civil Services Capacity Building), approved in September 2020. He stated that the iGOT Karmayogi digital learning portal now has over 1.7 crore registered users, hosts more than 5,600 courses (6,953 learning hours) in 23 languages, and has recorded over 14.42 crore course completions. Employees from central, state/UT, and local body levels are being onboarded, with Capacity Building Plans being prepared for all Ministries/Departments/Organisations, monitored by DoPT, the Capacity Building Commission, and Karmayogi Bharat SPV.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Government Policies and Interventions
GS Paper 4 - Ethics and Human Interface (Civil Service Values)

title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: STRENGTHENING OF CPGRAMS

ministry.name: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions

summary: In a written Lok Sabha reply, Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh detailed measures taken to strengthen CPGRAMS, including the Grievance Redressal Assessment Index (GRAI), Bhashini-based multilingual support, the 'Samadhan Didi' AI chatbot, reduction of disposal timeline from 30 to 21 days, and a Review Meeting Module for senior-level oversight. Data shared showed that in 2025-26, over 18.3 lakh grievances were received and 18.1 lakh disposed of, with average disposal time improving to 14 days from 16 days in 2023-24. The Government also issued Comprehensive Guidelines on Handling of Public Grievances in August 2024 and is developing 'NextGen CPGRAMS' using AI/ML for further improvement.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Citizens' Charters and grievance redressal mechanisms

title: Government Expands Citizen-Centric Digital Public Service Delivery through UMANG and DigiLocker
summary: The Ministry of Electronics & IT informed Rajya Sabha that as of 31 July 2026, about 2,575 services (880 Central, 1,695 State) are available on UMANG and 5,437 document types/services (661 Central, 4,776 State) on DigiLocker. UMANG has over 11.66 crore registered users with about 798 crore transactions in the last three years, while DigiLocker has over 72.43 crore registered users with about 72.86 crore document access transactions in the last three years. The government also highlighted expansion of Common Service Centres (CSCs), with 4,07,122 functional at the Gram Panchayat level as of 30 June 2026, including 70,069 run by women Village Level Entrepreneurs.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Government Policies and Interventions

title: MeitY's SAMRIDH Programme Supports 5 Startups through Accelerator-led Innovation; ₹1.81 Crore Disbursed under the Programme
