summary: In a Rajya Sabha reply dated 7 August 2026, MeitY Minister of State Jitin Prasada provided details of the SAMRIDH programme, which aimed to accelerate around 300 startups across sectors like Health-tech, Ed-tech, Agri-tech and Fin-tech, and concluded on 31 January 2026. In Andhra Pradesh, out of 7 accelerators that applied, one accelerator - Kalpataru Centre of Excellence (CoE) by AIC STPINEXT Initiatives, Visakhapatnam - was selected and supported 5 startups, with ₹1.81 crore disbursed to it under the programme.

title: Government Strengthens Cyber Security Capacity of Women Officials through CyberShakti Programme
summary: The Ministry of Electronics & IT informed the Rajya Sabha that 978 women government officials, including police officers and cyber cell personnel, have been trained under the CyberShakti programme since its launch in October 2024. The two-year programme uses two-week virtual instructor-led training and one-week offline residential training, with Delhi (249) and Gujarat (81) among the top contributors. The government has noted the 2026 Standing Committee's recommendation to scale up the programme, and a working group on Cyber Security recommended a second phase in May 2026.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Role of parliamentary committees in policy oversight

title: Government Promotes Sustainable Growth of Data Centres through Energy-Efficient and Clean Energy Measures
summary: The Ministry of Electronics & IT informed Rajya Sabha that India's data centre capacity has grown from 375 MW in 2020 to about 1575 MW currently, driven by rising AI and high-performance computing demand. CEA estimates data centre power demand could reach 17 GW by 2031-32. The government is promoting energy efficiency and clean energy for data centres through renewable energy schemes, the SHANTI Act for nuclear power, BIS standards, and energy conservation building codes.

title: Prime Minister highlights India’s strong conservation efforts on World Elephant Day
summary: On World Elephant Day (12 August 2026), Prime Minister Narendra Modi highlighted India's elephant conservation efforts, noting that India hosts over 60% of the world's wild Asian elephants and has 33 Elephant Reserves that provide habitats and support long-term conservation. He praised forest personnel, scientists, veterinarians, mahouts, and local communities for their contributions to these efforts.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 3 - Environment and Ecology: Wildlife Conservation
GS Paper 3 - Environment and Ecology: Biodiversity Conservation Efforts and Programmes
GS Paper 2 - Government Policies and Interventions

title: PMMSY IN CHHATTISGARH

ministry.name: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying

summary: In a Rajya Sabha reply, Union Minister Rajiv Ranjan Singh (Lalan Singh) informed that under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY), projects worth Rs. 956.86 crore (central share Rs. 321.01 crore) were approved for Chhattisgarh during 2020-21 to 2025-26, of which Rs. 274.16 crore was released. Key interventions include fish seed hatcheries, new fish ponds, biofloc units, cages, an Integrated Aqua Park, and welfare measures like insurance and Kisan Credit Cards for fishers. As a result, fish production in the state rose from 3.14 lakh metric tonnes in 2014-15 to 8.73 lakh metric tonnes in 2024-25.

title: HOLISTIC DEVELOPMENT OF FISHERIES

ministry.name: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying

summary: The Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying informed the Rajya Sabha about steps taken for holistic development of India's fisheries sector, which contributed about 7.43% to Agricultural GVA and 1.09% to total GVA in 2023-24. Key initiatives include PMMSY, FIDF, PM-MKSSY, and Kisan Credit Card facility extended to fishers since 2018-19. PM-MKSSY notably offers a one-time incentive of 40% of aquaculture insurance premium (with caps of ₹25,000/hectare or ₹1 lakh per farmer for 4 hectares WSA, and similar caps for intensive systems), with an additional 10% incentive for SC/ST and women beneficiaries.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Government Policies and Interventions

title: PROBLEMS FACED BY AQUA FARMERS

ministry.name: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying

summary: In response to a Rajya Sabha question, the Fisheries Minister informed that Andhra Pradesh has about 2.16 lakh aqua farmers covering 5.79 lakh acres, facing distress from falling market prices and rising feed costs. Andhra Pradesh negotiated a Rs.4/kg cut in shrimp feed prices and offers subsidised electricity at Rs.1.50/unit to registered aqua farmers, while confirming no state-wide crop holiday has been declared. The Centre has also rationalised customs duties on 16 aquaculture inputs (30% down to 0-5%) via Union Budgets 2024-25 and 2025-26, and cut GST on over 20 fisheries/aquaculture products from 12-18% to 5% in September 2025.

title: PROTECTION OF TRADITIONAL FISHING RIGHTS AND LIVELIHOODS

ministry.name: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying

summary: In a written reply to the Rajya Sabha, Union Minister Rajiv Ranjan Singh (Lalan Singh) detailed government measures to protect traditional fishing rights, including State Marine Fishing Regulation Acts reserving near-shore zones for artisanal fishers, satellite tracking of mechanized vessels under PMMSY, the new Sustainable Harnessing of Fisheries in the EEZ Rules 2025, and a uniform 61-day annual fishing ban during breeding season. It also described livelihood support schemes such as accidental insurance, sea ranching, artificial reefs, mariculture promotion, and development of 100 Climate Resilient Coastal Fishermen Villages.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 3 - Environment and Ecology: Marine Conservation and Blue Economy
GS Paper 2 - Centre-State Relations (Marine Fishing Regulation)

title: SALIENT FEATURE OF PM-MKSSY

ministry.name: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying

summary: The Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying detailed the salient features of Pradhan Mantri Matsya Kisan Samridhi Sah-Yojana (PM-MKSSY), a Rs. 6,000 crore Central Sector Sub-scheme under PMMSY running from FY2023-24 to FY2026-27. It covers formalization of the unorganized fisheries sector, institutional finance access, cooperative strengthening, aquaculture insurance incentives, and performance grants for microenterprises and value-chain development, aiming to generate 1.70 lakh jobs nationwide, including in Andhra Pradesh, without district-specific targets.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 3 - Government Schemes and their implementation

title: ACCESS PASS FOR FISHING IN INDIA'S EEZ

ministry.name: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying

summary: The Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying informed the Rajya Sabha that 9,650 free digital 'Access Passes' have been issued via the ReALCRaft Portal for fishing in India's Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ), under the Sustainable Harnessing of Fisheries in the EEZ Rules, 2025 (notified 4 November 2025). The pass is mandatory for mechanized vessels/large motorized boats over 24 metres fishing beyond 12 nautical miles, while small traditional crafts are exempt. Karnataka and Gujarat lead in passes issued, and complementary measures include duty-free treatment of EEZ-caught fish (Union Budget 2026-27) and integration with MPEDA, EIC, and Nabhmitra safety systems.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Government Policies and Interventions

title: Development of Tribal Communities under PMJUGA
summary: The Union Minister for Tribal Affairs informed the Rajya Sabha about progress under the Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Unnat Gram Abhiyan (PM-JUGA), also called Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (DAJGUA), launched on 2 October 2024. The scheme involves 25 interventions across 17 ministries aiming to saturate infrastructure gaps in 63,843 villages across 549 districts and 2,911 blocks in 30 States/UTs, benefiting over 5 crore tribals over five years. The release provided physical progress data (housing, roads, water, electrification, health, education) and state-wise fund releases, with Odisha, Assam, and Madhya Pradesh among top recipients.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Government Policies and Interventions

title: “DBT Tribal Portal and Tribal Scholarship Disbursement”
summary: In a Rajya Sabha reply, Union Minister for Tribal Affairs Durgadas Uikey detailed how the Ministry uses the DBT Tribal Portal to monitor and generate MIS reports for Pre-Matric and Post-Matric Scholarship Schemes for ST students, implemented as Centrally Sponsored Schemes through States/UTs. He highlighted digitization measures including the SNA SPARSH 'Just-in-Time' disbursement model that transfers central and state scholarship shares directly to student accounts to eliminate fund parking and delays, alongside integration with NSP, PFMS, and various dashboards. Annexure data showed beneficiary numbers fluctuating across states from FY2023-24 to 2025-26, with Pre-Matric totals of ~6.36 lakh, ~9.52 lakh, and ~7.40 lakh, and Post-Matric totals declining from ~17.84 lakh to ~15.91 lakh.

title: Tribal programmes in Tamil Nadu
summary: Union Minister for Tribal Affairs Durgadas Uikey informed Rajya Sabha about Central schemes for tribal welfare in Tamil Nadu, including Pre- and Post-Matric Scholarships, Eklavya Model Residential Schools (8 EMRS functional), Article 275(1) grants, PM-JANMAN, Van Dhan Vikas Kendras, NSTFDC loans, and Grant-in-Aid to NGOs, with district-wise fund releases and beneficiary numbers for FY2023-24 to FY2025-26. The reply also detailed the newly launched Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (DAJGUA) and PM JANMAN mission for Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs).
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Government Policies and Interventions

title: Progress under PM JANMAN for development of PVTGs
summary: The Union Minister for Tribal Affairs informed the Rajya Sabha about progress under PM JANMAN (Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan), a scheme covering 75 Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs) across 18 states and one UT. As of 30 June 2026, the scheme has delivered various interventions across 9 ministries including over 4.8 lakh houses sanctioned, 3 lakh completed, road connectivity, water, health, education, electrification and livelihood support. A habitation-level survey via the PM Gati Shakti mobile app has also estimated PVTG population at about 48.5 lakh across over 12.3 lakh households.

title: Cultural identity, language and traditional rights of Scheduled Tribes
summary: In a Rajya Sabha reply, Union Tribal Affairs Minister Durgadas Uikey outlined the Ministry's efforts to preserve tribal cultural identity, languages and traditional rights, highlighting support to 29 Tribal Research Institutes (TRIs) including Jharkhand's TRI under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme 'Support to Tribal Research Institutes'. He mentioned digital initiatives like the TribeX platform (formerly Adi Sanskriti) showcasing Jharkhand's art forms such as Sohrai Painting, Dokra Craft and Jadupetia Chitrakar, and the AI-based translation tool 'Adi Vaani' supporting Santhali and Mundari languages. The Minister clarified that implementation of Fifth Schedule provisions, PESA 1996, and the Forest Rights Act 2006 remains primarily a State responsibility, with the Ministry providing policy guidance and TRIs providing research support.

title: TEXT OF THE OBSERVATION MADE BY THE HON'BLE CHAIRMAN, RAJYA SABHA REGARDING DISCOURTEOUS AND UNDIGNIFIED COMMENTS BEING MADE BY MEMBERS INTERRUPTING THE SPEECH OF OTHER MEMBERS IN THE HOUSE
summary: The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha issued an observation cautioning Members of Parliament against making discourteous and undignified comments while interrupting other Members' speeches in the House. He urged MPs to avoid hurting the sentiments of fellow Members and to respect India's diverse regional cultures and identities.

title: Status of forest rights claims
summary: Union Minister for Tribal Affairs Durgadas Uikey informed the Rajya Sabha on 12 August 2026 about the status of claims filed under the Forest Rights Act (FRA), 2006, as reported by States/UTs up to 30 June 2026. Across 20 states and 1 Union Territory implementing the Act, over 54 lakh claims (individual and community) have been received, of which about 25.4 lakh have been approved with titles distributed, 18.1 lakh rejected, and around 10.5 lakh still pending. The Ministry clarified that community-wise and district-wise segregated data is not maintained, as implementation is the responsibility of State Governments/UT Administrations while MoTA only compiles monthly progress reports.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Government Policies and Interventions

title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: AI-Based Early Warning System
summary: In a written Lok Sabha reply, the Minister of State for Earth Sciences Dr. Jitendra Singh detailed the Government's use of AI, ML and Big Data to strengthen weather forecasting and early warning systems. Key initiatives include NCMRWF's integration of AI/ML with Numerical Weather Prediction, IITM Pune's AI/ML Centre, the 'meteoGAN' downscaling model for Delhi-NCR, and the 'MausamVani' and upcoming 'MausamGPT' LLM-based tools for multilingual advisories. Under Mission Mausam, an AI/ML hybrid model disseminated agronomic monsoon onset SMS advisories to about 5.28 crore farmers across 15 states and one UT during the 2026 southwest monsoon.

title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: SOUTH-WEST MONSOON FORECAST
summary: In a written Lok Sabha reply, MoS Earth Sciences Dr Jitendra Singh stated that IMD's 2026 monsoon forecast predicted below-normal rainfall (92% of LPA in April, revised to 90% in the second stage), linked to developing El Niño conditions. Actual cumulative seasonal rainfall as of 2 August 2026 stood at 12% below LPA, with June deficient by 35% and July slightly above normal at all-India level but spatially uneven. Sixteen meteorological subdivisions, including Bihar, Arunachal Pradesh, Assam & Meghalaya, and Punjab, recorded deficiencies between 20-38% below normal as of 5 August 2026.

title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: DEEP OCEAN MISSION
summary: In a Lok Sabha written reply, Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh stated that NIOT, Chennai has developed a deep-sea mining system that successfully underwent mobility and power trials at 5270 m depth in the Central Indian Ocean Basin (CIOB), a site allocated by the International Seabed Authority (ISA). The Ministry of Earth Sciences holds ISA exploration contracts for Polymetallic Nodules and Polymetallic Sulphides in international waters of the Indian Ocean, under which resource assessment, environmental impact studies, and baseline oceanographic surveys are being conducted. Currently, only exploration (not commercial mining) of deep seabed minerals is permitted under ISA rules.

title: Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi releases Autobiography of Former President Shri Ram Nath Kovind
summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi released the autobiography of former President Ram Nath Kovind, titled 'Triumph of the Indian Republic: My Life, My Struggles', at Vigyan Bhavan, New Delhi on 12 August 2026. Modi praised Kovind's journey from a humble background in Kanpur Dehat to the highest constitutional office, linking it to the egalitarian vision of Gandhi, Ambedkar, and the Phules. He also highlighted Kovind's continued post-presidential work on the 'One Nation, One Election' initiative.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Indian Polity: Constitutional posts (President, Governor)

title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: ADVANCED MARINE STATION FOR OCEAN BIOLOGY
summary: In a written Lok Sabha reply, Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh stated that CMLRE (Kochi), under the Ministry of Earth Sciences, has conducted about 19 surveys during 2023-2026 to assess fishery resources and marine biodiversity in India's Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ). The data supports sustainable marine living resource management, identification of Ecologically & Biologically Significant Areas (ESBAs), fishery yield estimation, genomic reference libraries, and reporting for international commitments like the CBD and SDG-14. Initiatives include the Bhavasagara National Repository for deep-sea specimens and long-term ecosystem monitoring under the MLR Programme.

title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: Status of Early Warning Systems
summary: In a written Lok Sabha reply, the Minister of State for Earth Sciences detailed India's expanded early warning infrastructure under Mission Mausam, including 50 Doppler Weather Radars, 1,008 Automatic Weather Stations, and 6,885 rain gauges that have improved severe weather forecast accuracy by 40-50% over a decade. It also covered INCOIS's role as Tsunami Service Provider for 28 Indian Ocean Rim nations, the new MHEW-DSS digital forecasting platform, Himalayan glacier and hazard research (including NCPOR's Himansh station and IITM's Gangotri-Gaumukh expedition), expansion of the seismological network from 86 to 174 observatories since 2014, and a ₹270 crore FY2026-27 budget for NCPOR's PACER scheme.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 3 - Environment and Climate Change
GS Paper 2 - Government Policies and Interventions

title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: FLOOD FORECASTING AND EARLY WARNING SYSTEM IN NORTHEAST INDIA
summary: In a written Lok Sabha reply, the Union Minister of State for Earth Sciences detailed how IMD provided 7-day lead-time district-level rainfall forecasts and daily colour-coded warnings for Upper Assam before the heavy to very heavy rainfall of 18-20 July 2026, driven by a monsoon trough, low-pressure area, and multiple upper-air cyclonic circulations. The reply also gave region-wise forecast performance statistics (PC, POD, FAR, CSI) for West, South, Central and Northeast Assam across Day 1 to Day 5 lead times, and explained how ENSO/IOD inform seasonal outlooks while CWC handles operational flood forecasting using IMD inputs. It further noted new tools like the 6 km BharatFS model, 'Arunika' and 'Arka' supercomputing systems, and the MHEW-DSS under Mission Mausam to improve Northeast India's forecasting and early warning capability.

title: 88,209 EVs were subsidized in Madhya Pradesh in FY 2025-26 Under the PM E-DRIVE scheme
summary: In response to a Parliament question, the Ministry of Heavy Industries stated that 94,277 electric vehicles were deployed in Madhya Pradesh in FY 2025-26 under the PM E-DRIVE scheme, of which 88,209 (81,840 e-2Ws and 6,369 e-3Ws) received subsidies across the state's districts. No electric buses have been allocated to Madhya Pradesh under the scheme, and the Ministry does not centrally track disbursement details by manufacturer or purchaser. The release also outlined India's broader EV promotion ecosystem, including FAME-II, PLI-Auto, PLI-ACC, PM E-DRIVE, and PM e-Bus Sewa-PSM schemes.

title: World Elephant Day
summary: On World Elephant Day (12 August), a PIB backgrounder highlights India's elephant conservation achievements, noting India hosts nearly 60% of the world's wild Asian elephant population, estimated at 22,446 as per SAIEE 2021-25. It details Project Elephant's framework covering 33 Elephant Reserves (80,777 km²) and 150 corridors, DNA-based monitoring, railway safety measures that cut train-hit elephant deaths from 26 (2013) to 12 (2024), and regulatory tools like the Captive Elephant (Transfer or Transport) Rules 2024 and Gajah Suchana genetic database.

title: FAME India Scheme Phase-II: Progress in Electric Vehicle Adoption and Charging Infrastructure
summary: The Ministry of Heavy Industries provided a status update on India's electric vehicle promotion schemes, including FAME-II (2019-2024), PLI-Auto, PLI-ACC Battery Storage, PM E-DRIVE, and PM e-Bus Sewa PSM. FAME-II supported ~16.72 lakh EVs and 5,299 e-buses with ₹11,500 crore outlay, while newer schemes like PM E-DRIVE (₹10,900 crore) aim to incentivize 28.30 lakh EVs. The release also details supporting measures like reduced GST, green license plates, and road tax waivers, along with cumulative EV charger installations of 67,657 as of August 2026.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Government Policies and Interventions

title: Ministry of Heavy Industries, under the SAMARTH centres has trained approximately 33000 persons
summary: The Ministry of Heavy Industries has trained approximately 33,000 persons through its four SAMARTH (Smart Advanced Manufacturing and Rapid Transformation Hub) Centres, under the Scheme for Enhancement of Competitiveness in the Indian Capital Goods Sector. Additionally, the Common Engineering Facility Centre at the Welding Research Institute, BHEL Trichy, has trained over 8,500 persons in advanced welding technologies in the last three years. The release also cites complementary skilling data from the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship, including 27,31,699 candidates trained under PMKVY 4.0 and 12,53,158 ITI enrolments in Capital Goods & Manufacturing sector courses over the same period.

title: India Reaffirms Commitment to Elephant Conservation on World Elephant Day 2026

ministry.name: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

summary: On World Elephant Day 2026, Union Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav and MoS Kirti Vardhan Singh reaffirmed India's commitment to elephant conservation, highlighting that India has 33 Elephant Reserves across 14 states and 150 scientifically validated elephant corridors. They noted that nearly 60% of the world's wild Asian elephants live in India, and emphasized advanced population monitoring and measures to mitigate human-elephant conflict. The ministers described elephants as ecosystem engineers and living symbols of India's ecological heritage.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 1 - Indian Geography: Forests and Wildlife Distribution

title: English rendering of PM's speech during release of former President Shri Ram Nath Kovind's autobiography
summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi spoke at the release of former President Ram Nath Kovind's autobiography, titled 'Triumph of the Indian Republic: My Life, My Struggles', held in the presence of Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla and Mrs. Savita Kovind. The PM praised Kovind's humble origins in Kanpur Dehat, his personal struggles including his mother's death, his rise through education and public service to become President of India, and his continued work on the 'One Nation, One Election' initiative even after retiring from the presidency.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Indian Polity: Office of the President

title: Vice-President flags off Har Ghar Tiranga Bike Rally of MPs, commemorating 150 years of Vande Mataram
summary: Vice-President C. P. Radhakrishnan flagged off a Har Ghar Tiranga Bike Rally with Members of Parliament at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, marking 150 years of the National Song 'Vande Mataram'. The rally, organised by the Ministry of Culture, proceeded to the Major Dhyan Chand National Stadium as part of the Har Ghar Tiranga Abhiyan 2026. The Vice-President spoke about Vande Mataram's role in inspiring freedom fighters and highlighted contributions of Tamil Nadu freedom fighters like V.O. Chidambaram Pillai and Subramania Bharati.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Government Policies and Interventions

title: Prime Minister shares a Sanskrit Subhashitam, highlighting the power of winning hearts through vision, thoughts, words, and actions
summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi shared a Sanskrit Subhashitam (aphorism) on X, emphasizing that a person who wins people's hearts through vision, thoughts, words, and actions earns trust, respect, and goodwill in return. He linked this message to praising India's youth, calling them not just the country's future but its greatest present strength, citing their sensitivity, service orientation, and capability that has given them a distinct global identity.

title: CCRAS-CARI Inaugurates Extension OPD Facility in New Delhi
summary: CARI (Central Ayurveda Research Institute), New Delhi, under CCRAS (Ministry of Ayush), inaugurated an Extension Outpatient Department (OPD) in Rohini, New Delhi on 11 August 2026. The facility, inaugurated by CCRAS Director General Prof. Rabinarayan Acharya, aims to expand access to evidence-based Ayurvedic outpatient healthcare services for residents of Rohini and adjoining areas. Senior CCRAS officials and CPWD representatives spoke about the clinical outreach and infrastructure aspects of the new centre.

title: GeM Strengthens Participation of MSMEs, Startups, Women Entrepreneurs and SHGs
summary: In a written Rajya Sabha reply on 11 August 2026, MoS Commerce & Industry Jitin Prasada gave data on GeM's registered MSMEs, startups, women entrepreneurs and SHGs as of 30 July 2026, and noted MSME procurement through GeM rose to ₹2.37 lakh crore in FY 2025-26. He also detailed GeM's use of AI/ML analytics and CCI's cartel-detection toolkit to flag suspicious procurement patterns, and disclosed seller suspension figures for the last three fiscal years due to incidents like wrong listings, unreasonable pricing and delivery delays.

title: PM GatiShakti National Master Plan Enables Integrated and Coordinated Infrastructure Planning
summary: The Ministry of Commerce & Industry informed Lok Sabha that PM GatiShakti National Master Plan (PMGS NMP), launched in October 2021, has evaluated 396 infrastructure projects worth about ₹18.66 lakh crore through its Network Planning Group, of which 256 are sanctioned and 198 under implementation. All 58 central Ministries/Departments and 36 States/UTs have been onboarded, and a public platform (ugi.pmgatishakti.gov.in) launched in September 2025 gives private entities and citizens access to data analytics. A DPIIT-NCAER 2025 study estimated India's logistics cost at 7.9% of GDP, comparable to advanced economies.

title: The Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development (Amendment) Bill, 2026
summary: Parliament passed the MSME Development (Amendment) Bill, 2026, updating the MSMED Act, 2006 to address payment delays, speed up dispute resolution, and simplify compliance for MSMEs. Key changes include mandatory TReDS-based invoice settlement for CPSEs, timelines for mediation and arbitration, voluntary and free registration for all MSMEs via a national digital platform, and decriminalisation of several minor offences. The Bill builds on the growing economic weight of the sector, which the Economic Survey 2025-26 says contributes 31.1% of GDP, 35.4% of manufacturing output and 48.58% of exports, with over 9.16 crore Udyam-registered enterprises employing more than 40 crore people.

title: IMPLEMENTATION OF DDU-GKY
summary: The Ministry of Rural Development informed Lok Sabha that DDU-GKY, a placement-linked skilling scheme under DAY-NRLM, has trained about 18.45 lakh and placed about 12.35 lakh rural youth since inception. Revised guidelines (DDU-GKY 2.0) rolled out from FY 2025-26 emphasize industry-led training, emerging sectors like EV maintenance and renewable energy, and long-term employment outcomes with a minimum 70% placement rate and one-year post-placement tracking. For FY 2026-27, ₹750 crore has been budgeted to train 1.37 lakh youth, with state-wise data shared for Madhya Pradesh and Gwalior Lok Sabha constituency.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Government Policies and Interventions

title: TARGET AND STATUS FOR CONSTRUCTION OF HOUSE UNDER PMAY-G
summary: The Ministry of Rural Development reported that under Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana-Gramin (PMAY-G), 32.47 lakh houses were sanctioned and 26.57 lakh completed in FY 2025-26. Cumulatively, against a total target of 4.18 crore houses, 3.91 crore have been sanctioned and 3.12 crore completed as of 3 August 2026, with 79 lakh houses under construction. The Minister of State also detailed convergence with schemes like Jal Jeevan Mission, PMUY, and PM-JANMAN, and reservation norms for SC/ST households and Special Projects.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Government Policies and Interventions

title: INTEGRATED MASTER PLAN FOR RURAL INFRASTRUCTURE
summary: In a written Lok Sabha reply dated 11 August 2026, Minister of State for Rural Development Shri Kamlesh Paswan stated that MoRD implements PMGSY, Viksit Bharat-Guarantee for Rozgar & Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB-G RAM G), and DAY-NRLM across the country, including Bhind and Datia districts of Madhya Pradesh, to improve rural infrastructure, employment and livelihoods. He clarified that there is currently no proposal for a separate integrated master plan for rural infrastructure and livelihood development for each Lok Sabha Constituency. The reply also detailed the Ministry's multi-layered monitoring architecture, including Performance Review Committees, National Level Monitors, Common Review Missions, and DISHA committees chaired by MPs at the district level.

title: STUDY ON MIGRATION
summary: In a written Lok Sabha reply, the Minister of State for Rural Development stated that the Ministry does not maintain data on migration-prone areas but addresses rural migration indirectly through multi-dimensional development schemes. Key programme achievements cited include 4994.17 crore persondays generated under MGNREGS since 2006, 10.08 crore women mobilized into 92 lakh SHGs under DAY-NRLM since 2011, and 3.11 crore houses completed under PMAY-G since 2016. The reply also highlighted the newly enacted Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Aajeevika Mission (Gramin) Act, 2025, effective from 1 July 2026, which guarantees 125 days of wage employment to willing rural households.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Government Policies and Interventions

title: REVISED TARGET FOR CONSTRUCTION OF HOUSES UNDER PMAY-G
summary: The Ministry of Rural Development informed Lok Sabha that during FY2021-22 to FY2025-26, 2.13 crore houses were targeted under PMAY-G, of which 1.95 crore were sanctioned and 1.21 crore constructed, with Rs. 1,31,100.02 crore Central share released and Rs. 2,17,896.40 crore spent. PMAY-G aims to build 4.95 crore rural houses by 31.03.2029, with 4.18 crore already allocated as targets. Fund releases were withheld for Odisha and West Bengal due to irregularities; Odisha's funds have resumed after satisfactory corrective action, while West Bengal's Action Taken Report remains under examination since FY2022-23.

title: RURAL SCHEMES IMPLEMENTED FOR SHGS
summary: The Ministry of Rural Development informed Lok Sabha that under DAY-NRLM, 10.08 crore rural women have been mobilized into 92.30 lakh Self Help Groups (SHGs) across 28 States and 6 UTs. The scheme supports SHGs through collateral-free institutional credit, RSETIs and CMTCs for training, and has produced measurable income gains per independent evaluations by 3ie and NITI Aayog. The Lakhpati Didi initiative under DAY-NRLM has helped 3.46 crore women SHG members achieve annual incomes of Rs 1 lakh or more.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Government Policies and Interventions

title: Strengthening of Cooperative Institutions in Vellore
summary: In a written Lok Sabha reply, Union Home and Cooperation Minister Amit Shah detailed the Ministry of Cooperation's multi-layered monitoring mechanism (IMC, NLCC, SCDC, DCDC) for cooperative institutions, with specific data on Vellore district, Tamil Nadu. It highlighted the Cooperative Ranking Framework, PACS computerization progress, formation of new multipurpose PACS/dairy/fishery cooperatives, diversification of PACS business activities, and capacity-building training conducted via NCCT, NABARD and NCDC financial assistance figures for Tamil Nadu.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Federal Structure and Centre-State Relations
GS Paper 3 - Rural Development and Institutional Credit

title: PRECISION AGRICULTURE
summary: In a written Lok Sabha reply, the Minister of State for Agriculture and Farmers Welfare detailed ICAR's Network Programme on Precision Agriculture (NePPA), involving 16 ICAR institutes developing sensor, drone, satellite, AI and IoT-based technologies for crop, soil, aquaculture and livestock management. The reply cited concrete outcomes such as 38,402 agri-drone demonstrations covering 41,280 hectares benefiting 4,54,083 farmers, cropping intensity rising from 137% to 272% via precision irrigation, and livestock disease forecasting up to two months in advance through ICAR-NIVEDI's AI/GIS models. It also highlighted specific technologies like drone-based nano-fertilizer spraying, tank-based super-intensive shrimp farming, and wearable IoT sensors for livestock health monitoring.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Government Policies and Interventions

title: Storage Capacity in PACS
summary: In a written Lok Sabha reply, the Ministry of Cooperation informed that under the Decentralized Grain Storage Plan in the Cooperative Sector, 12 PACS/Cooperative Societies with a combined capacity of 0.52 lakh metric tonnes (LMT) have been identified across 12 districts, with detailed project reports prepared for all 13 projects, though construction is yet to begin. One godown of 1,500 MT capacity has already been completed at Kotwa Pandey PACS in Mirzapur, Uttar Pradesh. The reply also detailed financial incentives introduced to speed up implementation, including an extended AIF loan repayment period, extension of the Nabhsanrakshan credit guarantee to PACS, higher AMI capital subsidy, reduced margin money, and an effective loan interest rate of 1% for PACS.

title: CULTIVATION OF KALA NAMAK RICE
summary: The Ministry of Agriculture informed Lok Sabha that Kalanamak rice cultivation in Siddharthnagar, Uttar Pradesh has expanded significantly between 2018-2025, with production rising over five-fold, sale price rising from Rs 40/kg to Rs 150/kg, and farmer participation growing from 2,915 to 23,000. This growth has been supported by schemes like PMFME/ODOP, ICAR variety development, a Common Facility Centre, seed multiplication programs, and APEDA-facilitated exports branding it as 'Buddha Rice' targeting Buddhist-majority nations.

title: Financial Irregularities in Cooperative Societies
summary: In a Lok Sabha written reply, the Ministry of Cooperation shared National Cooperative Database (NCD) data showing 8.53 lakh cooperative societies in India, of which 6.63 lakh are functional, 1.41 lakh non-functional, and 49,177 under liquidation; of the functional ones, 5.95 lakh are audited and 68,020 are not. Separately, 115 Multi-State Cooperative Societies (MSCS) are under liquidation under the MSCS Act, 2002, with Rajasthan (26) and Maharashtra (23) having the highest numbers. The Ministry listed reforms since its 2021 inception—including the 2023 MSCS Act amendment, a Cooperative Rehabilitation Fund, PACS computerization, Model Byelaws, and inclusion of rural cooperative banks under RBI's Ombudsman Scheme—aimed at improving transparency and accountability in the sector.

title: ALLOCATION FOR FISHERIES SECTOR

ministry.name: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying

summary: In a Lok Sabha reply, Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying Minister Rajiv Ranjan Singh (Lalan Singh) detailed progress under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY, Rs. 20,750 crore outlay since 2020-21) and the Fisheries and Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund (FIDF, since 2018-19), which together have funded 184 fishing harbours/landing centres, 775 cold storages/ice plants, and thousands of fish transport and vending units. India's marine product exports rose to 19.72 lakh metric tonnes worth Rs. 73,890 crore (USD 8.46 billion) in 2025-26, reaching over 128 countries, with value-added products growing from 2% (2013-14) to 11% (2024-25) of exports. The Ministry also reported livestock disease control data, including crore-scale vaccination doses against FMD, Brucellosis, PPR, Classical Swine Fever and Lumpy Skin Disease, and a fall in livestock disease outbreaks from 132 in 2019 to 40 in 2025.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Government Policies and Interventions

title: MDoNER and CHEMEXCIL Organise Industry Summit on Prospects & Export of Agarwood Oil from India

ministry.name: Ministry of Development of North-East Region

summary: MDoNER and CHEMEXCIL jointly organised an Industry Summit in New Delhi on the prospects and export of Indian agarwood oil, bringing together industry, scientific institutions and policymakers. The event saw release of a 'Roadmap for Agarwood Export Promotion from the North Eastern Region', which holds over 96% of India's agarwood tree resources, primarily in Assam and Tripura. The initiative aims to shift the NER from being a raw-material supplier to becoming the branded origin and standard-setter for Indian oud in global markets.

title: STATUS OF PM-MKSSY

ministry.name: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying

summary: The Department of Fisheries provided a status update on the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Kisan Samridhi Sah-Yojana (PM-MKSSY), a ₹6,000 crore Central Sector Sub-scheme under PMMSY running from FY2023-24 to FY2026-27. As of 6 August 2026, about 35.92 lakh stakeholders had registered on the National Fisheries Digital Platform (NFDP), with progress reported across cooperative strengthening, aquaculture insurance, credit facilitation, and performance grants, along with state-wise enterprise support data.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Government Policies and Interventions
GS Paper 3 - Financial Inclusion and Institutional Credit

title: Cooperative Societies in Odisha
summary: As per the National Cooperative Database (as on 15.07.2026), Odisha has 8,667 cooperative societies, of which 8,063 are functional. The Ministry of Cooperation informed Lok Sabha that NCDC has disbursed financial assistance to Odisha's cooperative sector (₹4.07 crore in 2021-22 rising to ₹7.03 crore in 2025-26) across activities like FPOs, dairy, fisheries and marketing, while ₹25.07 crore has been released to Odisha under the Centrally Sponsored Project for Computerization of PACS, which now covers 79,630 PACS nationally with an outlay of ₹2,925.39 crore. The reply also listed several cooperative banking reforms undertaken since the Ministry's creation in 2021 under the 'Sahakar-se-Samriddhi' vision.

title: POST-HARVEST LOSS AND BYCATCH FROM MARINE FISHERIES

ministry.name: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying

summary: In a Lok Sabha reply, Union Minister Rajiv Ranjan Singh (Lalan Singh) stated that studies by NPC and ICAR-CIFT estimate post-harvest losses in Karnataka's marine fisheries at around 6-10%, while ICAR-CMFRI found bycatch levels of 20-40% depending on gear and craft type. Under PMMSY, the DoF has approved ₹1053.60 crore worth of fisheries development projects for Karnataka over the last five years and FY 2026-27, including cold chain infrastructure (ice plants, cold storages, transport units, fish kiosks) benefiting 171 beneficiaries. Additionally, modernization of Mangaluru, Gangolli, and Malpe fishing harbours has been approved, and Karnataka promotes square-mesh cod-end trawl nets and Turtle Excluder Devices for sustainable fishing.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Government Policies and Interventions

title: FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE UNDER PMMSY

ministry.name: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying

summary: In a Lok Sabha reply, Union Minister Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh detailed financial assistance under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY), noting ₹21,461.03 crore approved nationally (Central share ₹9,571.09 crore) and ₹2,328.89 crore for Andhra Pradesh since 2020-21. He also cited ICAR-CMFRI and Fishery Survey of India data showing no conclusive impact of climate variability and pollution on overall marine fish production, with 91.1% of assessed marine fish stocks being sustainable. Additional details covered the FIDF infrastructure fund, Group Accident Insurance Scheme coverage of 167.64 lakh fishers, and Andhra Pradesh-specific diesel subsidy and fishing-ban compensation payments.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Government Policies and Interventions

title: Cooperative University
summary: The Ministry of Cooperation informed Parliament about the Tribhuvan Sahkari University Act, 2025, which mandates a dedicated university to train manpower for the cooperative sector and standardise cooperative education. It also detailed NCDC's women-focused schemes (Swayam Shakti Sahakar Yojna, Nandini Sahakar, Yuva Sahakar Yojana) with disbursement of ₹190.16 crore to women cooperatives in Rajasthan in 2025-26, and outlined major digitalisation measures such as PACS computerisation (63,686 PACS onboarded, 54,707 declared e-PACS), the National Cooperative Database portal 3.0, and RBI-approved reforms allowing Urban Cooperative Banks greater branch expansion and doorstep banking.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 3 - Banking and financial sector reforms

title: PROMOTION OF INLAND FISHERIES EXPORT

ministry.name: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying

summary: In a Lok Sabha reply, Fisheries Minister Rajiv Ranjan Singh (Lalan Singh) detailed government measures to boost seafood exports from inland states, including a draft guidance document prepared with MPEDA, EIC and NFDB for export readiness. Under PMMSY and FIDF, ₹2,797 crore has been approved for cold chain and marketing infrastructure including 775 cold storages, 28,489 fish transport units and various markets/kiosks. The government is also piloting a ₹116.85 lakh ICAR-CIFRI drone project to transport live fish (already demonstrating 70 kg over 7 km), has signed an MoU with ONDC for digital marketplace access, and supported 2,195 Fish Farmer Producer Organizations with ₹544.85 crore outlay.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Government Policies and Interventions

title: OBJECTIVE OF AYUSH GRID
summary: The Ministry of Ayush informed Rajya Sabha that the Ayush Grid project is a comprehensive IT backbone digitizing service delivery across Ayush healthcare, research, education, drug administration and medicinal plants. Twenty-four e-governance platforms have been developed, including the master My Ayush Integrated Services Portal (MAISP), ABDM-compliant Ayush Hospital Management Information System (AHMIS), Ayush Anudan Portal, AI-enabled Ayush Research Portal (43,000+ publications), Ayush Nivesh Saarthi investment portal, and e-Charak marketplace for medicinal plants. Additional digital repositories like AMAR, SAHI and E-Medha digitize ancient Ayurvedic texts and manuscripts.

title: PROMOTION OF YOGA AND NATUROPATHY IN PUBLIC HEALTH
summary: The Ministry of Ayush runs an Information, Education and Communication (IEC) scheme to promote Ayush systems, including Yoga and Naturopathy, through Arogya Fairs, Yoga Fests/Utsavs, International Day of Yoga (21 June) and Naturopathy Day (18 November). In a written reply in Rajya Sabha, the Minister of State (I/C) for Ayush, Shri Prataprao Jadhav, shared expenditure details for these programmes from 2023-24 to 2025-26, showing a sharp rise in spending on International Day of Yoga from ₹24.16 crore to ₹57.38 crore. The outreach combines physical participation with digital engagement via social media platforms.

title: ESTABLISHMENT OF NEW AYUSH MEDICAL COLLEGES IN THE COUNTRY
summary: In a written Rajya Sabha reply, the Union Minister of State (I/C) for Ayush stated that since Public Health is a State subject, states/UTs are primarily responsible for establishing Ayush educational institutions, though the Centrally Sponsored National Ayush Mission (NAM) provides financial assistance for setting up new Ayush colleges where government-sector teaching capacity is inadequate. Based on Odisha's proposal, the Government Ayurvedic Medical College, Mayurbhanj was approved under NAM for FY 2025-26. The reply also listed all 17 states/UTs and their respective Ayush institutions supported under NAM from 2014-15 to 2026-27.

title: WELFARE SCHEMES FOR FISHERMEN

ministry.name: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying

summary: In a Lok Sabha reply, Union Minister Rajiv Ranjan Singh (Lalan Singh) detailed Central government fisheries welfare schemes implemented in Kerala, particularly Vadakara. Under PMMSY, Kerala has been approved Rs.1,413.91 crore worth of proposals (Rs.598.58 crore central share), with Rs.462.22 crore released and about 7,561 beneficiaries in Vadakara. Under FIDF, 13 projects worth Rs.551.72 crore have been approved statewide, though none specifically for Vadakara, while under PM-MKSSY's National Fisheries Digital Platform, 2,52,301 Kerala stakeholders (5,032 from Vadakara) have registered.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Government Policies and Interventions

title: FOCUS AREAS FOR STRENGTHENING AYUSH SECTOR
summary: The Ministry of Ayush, in a Rajya Sabha reply, outlined focus areas for strengthening the Ayush sector under Union Budget 2026-27, including setting up three new All India Institutes of Ayurveda, upgrading the WHO Global Traditional Medicine Centre in Jamnagar, caregiver training, inclusion of Ayush in Medical Value Tourism, and strengthening certification standards. The Ministry's total budget allocation for 2026-27 is Rs. 4408.93 crore, covering administrative expenses, statutory/autonomous bodies, Central Sector Schemes, and the Centrally Sponsored National Ayush Mission (NAM), under which Rs. 6,40,699.24 lakh has been released since 2014-15. The Ministry also stated it has given technical inputs to DPIIT for integrating Ayush into proposed regional medical hubs announced in the Budget, though no formal implementation proposals have been received yet.

title: PROMOTION OF SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH IN AYUSH SYSTEMS
summary: The Ministry of Ayush informed the Rajya Sabha about its initiatives to promote scientific research in Ayush systems, including the Ayurgyan Scheme (with its ABIHR component supporting 11 high-end research projects worth Rs.58.28 crore) and funding to five Research Councils (CCRAS, CCRH, CCRUM, CCRS, CCRYN) totaling hundreds of crores over FY2023-24 to FY2025-26. It also detailed international collaborations with WHO (including ICD-11 Traditional Medicine Module-2, WHO Global Traditional Medicine Centre in Jamnagar) and MoUs signed by CCRH, CCRUM and PCIM&H with foreign universities and institutions to promote global recognition of Ayush systems.

title: RESEARCH CAPACITY BUILDING IN AYURVEDA
summary: CCRAS (Central Council for Research in Ayurvedic Sciences), the apex Ayurveda research body under the Ministry of AYUSH, has undertaken multiple research capacity-building initiatives: the 'PRAYATNA' scheme to train PG/PhD Ayurveda scholars in scientific writing, a Digital Initiatives Dashboard consolidating CCRAS's web resources, accreditation of its institutes under NABH and NABL standards, and a new textbook on Research Methodology under the 'Ayurved Prabodhini' series. This information was presented by Union Minister of State (I/C) for AYUSH, Shri Prataprao Jadhav, in the Rajya Sabha.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Government Policies and Interventions

title: ASSISTANCE TO COASTAL FISHERMEN

ministry.name: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying

summary: The Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying informed the Lok Sabha that India's annual fish production rose from 147.25 lakh tonnes in 2020-21 to 197.75 lakh tonnes in 2024-25. It detailed key schemes for coastal fishermen's welfare and infrastructure development — PMMSY, FIDF, PMMKSSY, and Kisan Credit Card (KCC) facility for fishers — along with approved fishing harbour, landing centre, dredging, cold chain and marketing projects, and state-wise funding and beneficiary data under PMMSY from 2020-21 to 2025-26.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Government Policies and Interventions

title: Odisha’s Rare Earth Corridor, Marine Biotechnology and Space Capabilities to Drive New Opportunities for Science-led Growth: Dr Jitendra Singh
summary: Union Minister Dr Jitendra Singh met Odisha's Science & Technology Minister Krushna Chandra Patra to discuss an integrated science-led development roadmap for Odisha, covering rare earth exploration, marine biotechnology, space applications and life sciences infrastructure. Key outcomes include finalising the expansion of the Institute of Life Sciences, Bhubaneswar with an additional 50 acres from the State Government, plans to align the Odisha Marine Biotechnology Research & Innovation Corridor (OMBRIC) with Earth Sciences, CSIR and Biotechnology institutions, exploring a PPP-mode Space Research and Manufacturing Centre with ISRO, and taking forward Odisha's role in the Union Budget 2026-27's Rare Earth Corridor initiative alongside Kerala, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu.

title: DIGITAL GENERAL CROP ESTIMATION SURVEY
summary: The Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare informed the Lok Sabha that the Digital General Crop Estimation Survey (DGCES), piloted in Kharif 2023-24 in select districts of 10 states, expanded to 22 States/UTs in Rabi 2023-24, and is now operational across 23 States/UTs. DGCES digitizes Crop Cutting Experiments (CCEs) using a mobile app with geo-tagging, time-stamping and photographic evidence, and web-based dashboards for real-time monitoring. The information was shared by Minister of State Ramnath Thakur in a written reply.

title: MINISTER OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT, SMT. ANNPURNA DEVI MEETS PARLIAMENTARY DELEGATION FROM THE REPUBLIC OF LIBERIA AND THE WOMEN’S LEGISLATIVE CAUCUS OF LIBERIA

ministry.name: Ministry of Women and Child Development

summary: Union Minister for Women and Child Development Smt. Annpurna Devi met a Parliamentary delegation from Liberia, including members of the Senate, House of Representatives and the Women's Legislative Caucus, led by Ms. Ellen-Attoh Wreh, along with UN Women representatives, in New Delhi. The delegation is on a South-South Peer Learning Mission (10-15 August 2026) supported by UN Women and funded through the IBSA Fund (India, Brazil, South Africa). Discussions covered India's initiatives on women's political representation, gender-responsive governance and budgeting, violence against women, the care economy, and women's leadership in local governance.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - International Institutions: UN Women and multilateral cooperation

title: ADVANCES IN AGRICULTURE TECHNOLOGY
summary: In a written Lok Sabha reply, Minister of State Ramnath Thakur outlined the government's initiatives to promote agricultural technology, including mechanization under SMAM, drone usage, and digital infrastructure through the Digital Agriculture Mission. Key highlights include over 10.33 crore Farmer IDs generated under AgriStack, Digital Crop Survey covering 604 districts and 28.5 crore plots in Kharif 2025, and the BharatVistaar AI platform serving 5.9 lakh farmers with 93 lakh queries addressed. Research institutions like ICAR and SAUs are developing crop-specific machinery, while MIDH supports horticultural mechanization.

title: SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURAL PRACTICES
summary: In a written Lok Sabha reply on 11 August 2026, the Minister of State for Agriculture and Farmers Welfare detailed Central schemes promoting sustainable agriculture, including Soil Health Cards, Per Drop More Crop, PKVY/MOVCDNER for organic farming, Agroforestry Scheme, and the National Mission on Natural Farming (NMNF). It cited NITI Aayog evaluation data showing high farmer satisfaction across schemes and noted foodgrain production rose from 252.03 million tonnes (2014-15) to 357.73 million tonnes (2024-25), while horticulture output rose from 280.98 to 370.73 million tonnes over the same period.

title: NATIONAL FARM MECHANISATION POLICY
summary: In a written Lok Sabha reply, the Minister of State for Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Ramnath Thakur, detailed the government's farm mechanization framework centered on the Sub-Mission on Agricultural Mechanization (SMAM) under RKVY. The scheme provides 40-50% subsidy for machinery purchase, 40% for Custom Hiring Centres (up to Rs 250 lakh projects), and 80-95% for Farm Machinery Banks. The reply also covered the Crop Residue Management Scheme, MIDH horticulture mechanization support, 100% FDI in agri-machinery manufacturing, and clarified there is no dedicated mechanization partnership proposal with South Korea currently.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 3 - Agricultural mechanization, marketing, land reforms
GS Paper 2 - Government schemes and policies for vulnerable sections (small/marginal farmers)

title: TECHNOLOGY DRIVEN CROP MONITORING SYSTEM
summary: In a written Lok Sabha reply on 11 August 2026, the Minister of State for Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Ramnath Thakur, detailed the Government of India's technology-driven crop monitoring ecosystem, which uses satellites, drones, AI, GIS, IoT and remote sensing. Key initiatives include FASAL for crop production forecasting, YES-TECH and WINDS under PMFBY for yield estimation and weather data, Krishi-DSS for integrated geospatial decision-making, drone promotion schemes like SMAM and Namo Drone Didi, and AI platforms such as the National Pest Surveillance System, BharatVistaar, Kisan Sarathi, and AgriStack. The reply provided coverage figures such as 2,122 drones distributed under SMAM, 1,094 drones under Namo Drone Didi, 35,565 pest advisories issued, and over 2.97 crore farmers registered on Kisan Sarathi.

title: PDUNASS Inaugurates Joint EPFO–ITC-ILO Training Programme on “Actuarial Practices in Social Security: Strengthening Actuarial Governance at EPFO India”
summary: PDUNASS, EPFO's apex training institute, inaugurated a joint EPFO–ITC-ILO residential training programme on actuarial governance in New Delhi on 10 August 2026. The three-day residential phase (10-12 August 2026) follows an online module run via ITC-ILO e-Campus from 25 May to 9 August 2026, covering actuarial valuation methods, Asset-Liability Management, and global governance best practices. The programme was inaugurated by CPFC Shri Ramesh Krishnamurthi and attended by senior EPFO and ESIC officials along with ILO/ITC-ILO faculty.

title: Conferment of Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship (Akademi Ratna) & Sangeet Natak Akademi Awards (Akademi Puraskar) for the years 2024 and 2025
summary: The President of India will confer Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowships (Akademi Ratna) and Sangeet Natak Akademi Awards (Akademi Puraskar) for 2024 and 2025 upon 115 artists at a ceremony on 13 August 2026 at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi. The honourees span music, dance, theatre, folk/tribal arts, puppetry and allied art forms from across India's States and Union Territories. Fellows receive Rs 3 lakh purse money while Awardees receive Rs 1 lakh, along with a Tamrapatra and Angavastram, continuing a tradition of Akademi Awards conferred since 1952.

title: Union Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh Highlights Massive Growth in India's Livestock Sector

ministry.name: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying

summary: Union Minister Rajiv Ranjan Singh (Lalan Singh) highlighted growth in India's livestock sector, noting Kisan Credit Card (KCC) coverage for animal husbandry farmers rose to 50.42 lakh beneficiaries in FY 2025-26 from 15.08 lakh in 2021-22. India's milk production reached 247.87 million tonnes in 2024-25, exceeding domestic demand of 243 million tonnes, while dairy exports touched $407.18 million in FY 2025-26. The Ministry also detailed flagship schemes—Rashtriya Gokul Mission, National Livestock Mission, and Livestock Health and Disease Control Programme—including specific achievements in Tamil Nadu such as 245 Mobile Veterinary Units and disease control support.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Government Policies and Interventions

title: MISLEADING MOBILE APPLICATIONS
summary: In a written Lok Sabha reply, MoS Home Affairs Bandi Sanjay Kumar detailed the government's cybercrime infrastructure under the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C), including the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal, Sahyog Portal, and Citizen Financial Cyber Fraud Reporting and Management System (CFCFRMS). As of 30.06.2026, 3,718 fraudulent apps had been blocked, over Rs 11,158 crore saved across 32.80 lakh complaints via CFCFRMS, and a Suspect Registry had blocked lakhs of SIMs and IMEIs while flagging mule accounts worth Rs 25,698 crore in declined transactions. The Ministry also issued a new SOP for complaint processing and fund restoration, and listed multiple public awareness campaigns against cyber fraud.

title: Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation Organises 11th District Collectors’ Peyjal Samvad
summary: The Department of Drinking Water & Sanitation held the 11th District Collectors' Peyjal Samvad via video conference, chaired by Secretary Ashok K.K. Meena, to review progress under Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) 2.0 and share best practices. Four districts—Uttara Kannada (Karnataka), Khowai (Tripura), Didwana Kuchaman (Rajasthan), and Chatra (Jharkhand)—presented innovative practices on source sustainability, IEC-based behaviour change, grievance redressal, and convergence with schemes like MGNREGA and VB-G RAM G. Officials also discussed the 'Sujalam Shakti' roadmap for women-led water quality monitoring and noted that over 2 lakh villages and 1 lakh Gram Panchayats have achieved Har Ghar Jal certification.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Issues relating to development and management of Social Sector/Services (drinking water, sanitation)

title: URBAN FLOOD RISK MITIGATION PROGRAMME
summary: The Ministry of Home Affairs informed the Lok Sabha that the Union Government has approved the Urban Flood Risk Management Programme (UFRMP) in two phases: Phase-I covering 7 cities (Ahmedabad, Bengaluru, Chennai, Hyderabad, Kolkata, Mumbai, Pune) with an outlay of Rs 3075.65 crore, and Phase-II covering 11 cities (Bhopal, Bhubaneshwar, Guwahati, Jaipur, Kanpur, Patna, Raipur, Trivandrum, Vishakhapatnam, Indore, Lucknow) with an outlay of Rs 2444.42 crore, funded under the National Disaster Mitigation Fund (NDMF). All Phase-I city projects and Guwahati under Phase-II are under implementation, aimed at improving stormwater drainage and urban flood resilience, with NDMA monitoring progress via a Monitoring and Evaluation Framework.

title: E-FIR UNDER BNSS
summary: The Ministry of Home Affairs informed the Lok Sabha that Section 173 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023 allows information about a cognizable offence to be given either orally or through electronic communication to a police officer, regardless of jurisdiction. Oral information must be recorded in writing and signed by the informant, while electronic information (e-FIR) must be signed by the informant within three days for it to be officially taken on record. This was stated by MoS Home Affairs Bandi Sanjay Kumar in a written reply.

title: TRAINING INSTITUTES FOR CAPFs
summary: In a written Lok Sabha reply, MoS Home Affairs Nityanand Rai stated that 83 Training Institutions of Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs) have been established across India, with ongoing expansion, modernization and upgradation of these centres including procurement of vehicles and technical gadgets. The government has also decided to set up a Central Jungle Warfare College (CRPF) in Bijapur, Chhattisgarh, and a Regional Training Centre (CISF) in Kishanganj, Bihar.

title: INSTITUTE OF FORENSIC SCIENCE
summary: The Ministry of Home Affairs informed the Lok Sabha that the National Forensic Sciences University (NFSU), established by an Act of Parliament in 2020 as an Institution of National Importance, initially had campuses in Gandhinagar (Gujarat) and Delhi. The government has since approved 14 additional NFSU campuses across states including Goa, Tripura, Madhya Pradesh, Karnataka, Assam, Maharashtra, Odisha, Chhattisgarh, Tamil Nadu, Rajasthan, Andhra Pradesh, West Bengal, Bihar, and Uttar Pradesh. NFSU has also set up training academies in Imphal (Manipur) and Pune (Maharashtra).

title: STRENGTHENING NARCO COORDINATION CENTRE
summary: The Ministry of Home Affairs informed the Lok Sabha that the 4-tier Narco-Coordination (NCORD) mechanism—Apex, Executive, State and District levels—has been restructured and strengthened to improve inter-ministerial and inter-agency coordination against drug trafficking. So far, 10 Apex, 7 Executive, 272 State and 16,187 District NCORD meetings have been held, feeding into a Vision Document on Narcotics Control (2026-2029) by the Narcotics Control Bureau. Related initiatives include the NCORD Portal (a knowledge management system), the MANAS 24x7 helpline (1933), the NIDAAN database of arrested narco-offenders, and Mission SPANDAN involving spiritual institutions in anti-drug awareness.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 3 - Government Schemes and Initiatives related to Narcotics Control

title: INCIDENTS OF CLOUDBURSTS
summary: In a written Lok Sabha reply, MoS Home Affairs Nityanand Rai stated that a Multi-Sectoral Central Team (MSCT) has been constituted to study the rising frequency of cloudbursts, flash floods, landslides and extreme rainfall in Himachal Pradesh. The team includes experts from NDMA, CBRI Roorkee, IITM Pune, and IIT Indore, with inputs from IMD, CWC and GSI. It will scientifically assess causes, examine ground conditions in worst-affected areas, and recommend long-term mitigation measures. The MSCT's findings link the trend to climate change-driven extreme rainfall, accelerated snowmelt, moraine instability, and anthropogenic factors.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 3 - Environment and Climate Change

title: DEVELOPMENT OF NEW WATERWAY CORRIDORS ACROSS THE COUNTRY

ministry.name: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways

summary: The Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways informed Rajya Sabha that of 111 National Waterways declared under the National Waterways Act, 2016, only 32 are currently operational for cargo and passenger movement. Following the 2026-27 budget announcement, 19 additional new National Waterways spanning states like Jammu & Kashmir, Karnataka, Goa, Odisha, Kerala, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Himachal Pradesh, Punjab and Uttar Pradesh have been identified for phased development between FY 2026-27 and FY 2030-31, primarily for cruise tourism and passenger ferry operations. The government stated its priority is to first develop existing feasible waterways before declaring further new ones.

title: NATIONAL WATERWAYS DEVELOPMENT PROGRAMME

ministry.name: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways

summary: The Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways informed the Rajya Sabha about development works on National Waterway-4 (Krishna river), including a Ro-Ro terminal built at Muktyala, four floating jetties handed to Andhra Pradesh Tourism Development Corporation, and a new Ro-Ro terminal awarded at Harishchandrapuram. Fund allocation for NW-4 rose from Rs 0.67 crore in 2023-24 to Rs 18.28 crore in 2025-26, while cargo movement was 5.71 Million Tonnes and passenger movement 2.34 Million in 2025-26. The reply also flagged challenges such as land transfer delays, seasonal water depth variation due to Pulichintala Dam releases, and low-level bridges, old locks and encroachments hampering navigation.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 3 - Inland Waterways and Transport
GS Paper 2 - Government Policies and Interventions

title: SAGARMALA PROJECT, NATIONAL WATERWAYS AND COASTAL SHIPPING

ministry.name: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways

summary: In a written Rajya Sabha reply, the Union Minister of Ports, Shipping and Waterways stated that the National Productivity Council conducted a third-party impact evaluation of Sagarmala scheme projects, with no projects sanctioned under its port-led industrialization pillar. National Waterways cargo movement reached 218 million metric tons in FY 2025-26, average turnaround time at Major Ports improved to 48.84 hours (from 52.87 hours in FY 2021-22), and Jawaharlal Nehru Port ranked 22nd in the World Bank's CPPI 2025. The Ministry also listed policy measures to boost coastal shipping and inland waterways, including the Jalvahak incentive scheme, the Coastal Cargo Promotion Scheme (targeting 12% combined modal share by 2047), development of National Waterway-5 in Odisha, tonnage tax extension to inland vessels, and new regulations enabling private investment in inland waterway terminals.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 3 - Government Policies and Interventions
GS Paper 1 - Indian Geography: River Systems and Waterways

title: SAGARMALA STARTUP AND INNOVATION INITIATIVE

ministry.name: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways

summary: The Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways informed the Rajya Sabha about the Sagarmala Startup and Innovation Initiative (S2I2), launched on 19.03.2025 to build a maritime innovation ecosystem, implemented by the Maritime India Foundation (MIF). Four Maritime Innovation Hubs have been set up at IIT Madras, IIT Bombay, IIT Kharagpur and IMU Chennai, and India's first Maritime Hackathon, MAR-a-THON 2025, was held with 330 startup applications for 51 problem statements, resulting in 36 startups selected for 40 projects. Visakhapatnam Port identified 4 problem statements, and 2 Andhra Pradesh startups have been onboarded to address them.

title: LIGHTHOUSE TOURISM AND MARITIME HERITAGE

ministry.name: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways

summary: The Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways informed the Rajya Sabha that the government is promoting Lighthouse Tourism under Section 23 of the Marine Aids to Navigation Act, 2021, alongside lighthouses' core navigation function. Lighthouse Museums have been set up at Chennai, Mahabalipuram, Alappuzha, Kannur, Muttom, Dwarka and Gopnath, and tourism facilities such as cafeterias, gardens, light and sound shows, and amphitheatres have been developed at 75 lighthouses across coastal states and Union Territories. The information was shared by Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal in a written reply.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Government Policies and Interventions
GS Paper 3 - Maritime and Coastal Development (Sagarmala)

title: Bulk Drug Park in Odisha

ministry.name: Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers :Department of Pharmaceuticals

summary: In a written Rajya Sabha reply, the Minister of State for Chemicals and Fertilizers, Anupriya Patel, clarified that no Bulk Drug Park has been proposed or approved for Odisha under the Centre's scheme for Promotion of Bulk Drug Parks or under the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme. Under the Bulk Drug Parks scheme, approved by the Cabinet on 20 March 2020 to set up three parks nationally, proposals were received from thirteen states but only those from Gujarat, Himachal Pradesh, and Andhra Pradesh were approved.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Government Policies and Interventions

title: Regulation and rationalisation of maximum retail prices of medicines

ministry.name: Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers :Department of Pharmaceuticals

summary: In a written Rajya Sabha reply, the Minister of State for Chemicals and Fertilizers, Anupriya Patel, explained how drug prices are regulated under the Drugs (Prices Control) Order (DPCO) 2013 by the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA), based on the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Policy 2012. She noted that out-of-pocket health expenditure as a share of Total Health Expenditure fell from 62.6% in 2014-15 to 43.4% in 2022-23, aided by price control and schemes like Janaushadhi Pariyojana, AB-PMJAY, Free Drugs Service Initiative, and AMRIT. The reply detailed ceiling price mechanisms for scheduled drugs, the 10% annual cap on non-scheduled drug price hikes, and NPPA's compliance monitoring mechanisms.

title: National Green Hydrogen Mission Advances Green Hydrogen Adoption in Petroleum and Refining Sector

ministry.name: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy

summary: The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy informed the Rajya Sabha that under the SIGHT Mode-2B scheme of the National Green Hydrogen Mission, 30 KTPA of green hydrogen production capacity has been awarded to four refineries: IOCL Panipat (10 KTPA), BPCL Bina (5 KTPA), HPCL Vizag (5 KTPA), and Numaligarh Refineries (10 KTPA). These projects will be implemented via Build-Own-Operate (BOO) arrangements by private developers with project-specific investments. The initiative aims to reduce dependence on imported fossil fuels and support India's energy security and net-zero goals.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Government Policies and Interventions

title: Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Kendras

ministry.name: Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers :Department of Pharmaceuticals

summary: As of 30 June 2026, 20,149 Jan Aushadhi Kendras (JAKs) have been opened across India under the Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana (PMBJP), including 1,833 in Kerala. The scheme's product basket includes 2,110 medicines and 315 surgicals/consumables, and over FY2021-22 to FY2025-26 it generated sales of Rs. 7,873.85 crore, saving citizens an estimated Rs. 37,200 crore. The Minister of State for Chemicals and Fertilizers detailed the franchise model for opening JAKs, supply-chain measures, and quality assurance mechanisms in a Rajya Sabha written reply.

title: Shortages of essential medicines in Government hospitals and Jan Aushadhi Kendras

ministry.name: Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers :Department of Pharmaceuticals

summary: In a written Rajya Sabha reply, the Minister of State for Chemicals and Fertilizers stated that the government runs the Free Drugs Service Initiative (FDSI) under the National Health Mission to provide free essential medicines at public health facilities, and monitors medicine availability at Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Kendras (JAKs) through PMBI. The reply detailed facility-wise Essential Medicines Lists, quality assurance mechanisms, a Central Dashboard (DVDMS) for monitoring, and steps like incentivizing stocking of 200 commonly used medicines at JAKs since September 2024 to address supply gaps.

title: Expansion of PM Jan Aushadhi Kendras in West Bengal and coverage of uncovered blocks

ministry.name: Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers :Department of Pharmaceuticals

summary: In a written Rajya Sabha reply, the Minister of State for Chemicals and Fertilizers stated that the Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Bureau of India (PMBI) has not received any proposal from the West Bengal government for opening 469 new Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Kendras (JAKs). As of 30 June 2026, West Bengal had 1,014 JAKs, of which 715 are spread across 217 of the state's 345 development blocks, leaving 128 blocks without any Jan Aushadhi Kendra. District- and block-wise data were provided, showing concentration in urban/peri-urban districts like North 24 Parganas, Kolkata, Hooghly and Howrah, and gaps mainly in blocks of Murshidabad, Purulia, Birbhum and Malda.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Centre-State relations in scheme implementation

title: Jan Aushadhi Kendras

ministry.name: Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers :Department of Pharmaceuticals

summary: The Department of Pharmaceuticals informed the Rajya Sabha that 20,149 Jan Aushadhi Kendras (JAKs) have been opened across India under the Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana (PMBJP) scheme as of 30 June 2026. Uttar Pradesh leads with 4,226 kendras, followed by Kerala (1,833) and Karnataka (1,720), while smaller UTs like Lakshadweep (1) and Ladakh (3) have minimal presence. This information was provided by Minister of State Smt. Anupriya Patel in a written reply.

title: LOW PARTICIPATION IN GRAM SABHA MEETINGS
summary: The Ministry of Panchayati Raj released a National Study Report prepared by NIRDPR on 30 June 2026 identifying reasons for low and inconsistent participation in Gram Sabha meetings, including livelihood constraints, poor awareness, weak grievance redressal, and gender-specific barriers to women's participation. In a written reply to the Lok Sabha on 11 August 2026, Minister Rajiv Ranjan Singh detailed several ongoing measures such as the Revamped RGSA scheme, Shashakta Panchayat Netri Abhiyan, Model Youth Gram Sabha, People's Plan Campaign, and digital tools like eGramSwaraj and Panchayat NIRNAY to strengthen Gram Sabha functioning.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Government Policies and Interventions

title: E-GRAM SWARAJ AND AUDITONLINE
summary: The Ministry of Panchayati Raj informed the Lok Sabha that under the e-Panchayat Mission Mode Project, it has developed eGramSwaraj and AuditOnline portals for digital planning, budgeting, accounting, audit and asset management of Panchayats. eGramSwaraj is integrated with PFMS, GeM, BHASHINI, BSNL/BharatNet and IMD, and as of FY 2025-26 over 2.5 lakh Village Panchayats are onboarded on the PFMS interface with over 2.5 lakh GPDPs uploaded. The Ministry also shared state-wise audit report generation data for FY 2024-25 and RGSA capacity-building training figures for Panchayat functionaries from 2022-23 to 2026-27.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Panchayati Raj Institutions and 73rd Constitutional Amendment
GS Paper 2 - Government Policies and Interventions
GS Paper 3 - Role of digital technology in public financial management and transparency

title: DHR-ICMR’s SHINE 2026 brings school students face-to-face with health research across 83 locations

ministry.name: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

summary: The Department of Health Research (DHR) and ICMR launched the second edition of ICMR-SHINE (Science and Health Innovation for NextGen Explorers) on 11-12 August 2026, a two-day open-day programme across 83 ICMR institutes, Model Rural Health Research Units and field units nationwide. Around 30,000 students from Grades 9-12 are participating in lab tours, exhibitions, poster walks and interactions with scientists, inspired by PM Modi's call to 'spend one day as a scientist'. ICMR also launched the SHINE website and announced a nationwide student research competition to encourage young learners to frame research questions on public health challenges.

title: Prime Minister shares an article by Union Minister on GeM transforming public procurement
summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi shared an article by Union Minister Piyush Goyal on X highlighting the achievements of the Government e Marketplace (GeM) over the past decade. He praised GeM for enabling transparent procurement, wider participation, and better opportunities, noting it has strengthened Ease of Doing Business by creating a competitive, inclusive ecosystem that particularly empowers MSMEs and women entrepreneurs.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Government Policies and Interventions

title: ALLOCATION OF FUNDS FOR STARTUPS
summary: The Ministry of Textiles informed the Lok Sabha that under the National Technical Textiles Mission (NTTM), the GREAT scheme has approved 31 start-up projects at a total cost of Rs 15.40 crore, of which Rs 13.65 crore is the Government of India's share. The NTTM's total budget for 2026-27 is Rs 256 crore, and Telangana alone has had 15 research projects and one academic institution application approved under related NTTM guidelines. The information was given by Minister of State for Textiles Shri Pabitra Margherita in a written reply.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Government Policies and Interventions
GS Paper 3 - Startups and Entrepreneurship Ecosystem

title: TEXTILE RECYCLING AND CIRCULAR ECONOMY
summary: In a written Lok Sabha reply, the Minister of State for Textiles outlined government measures to promote textile recycling and a circular economy, including the Union Budget 2026-27's 'Tex-Eco Initiative', a study mapping India's textile waste value chain, an ESG Task Force, and various international and domestic projects like UNIDO-GEF, UNEP In-Tex India, NTTM support, PM MITRA Parks sustainability framework, and promotion of upcycled products via GeM procurement.
syllabus_topics: GS Paper 2 - Government Policies and Interventions

title: Ship Recycling in India: Regulatory Transformation and Global Leadership
summary: India became the world's leading ship recycling nation in 2025, with its global market share rising from 30.1% to 35.4% and recycling volume increasing nearly 60%, from 1.86 million GT to 2.99 million GT, according to UNCTAD data. This achievement meets the Maritime India Vision (MIV) 2030 target five years ahead of schedule. The Alang-Sosiya cluster in Gujarat, handling about 98% of India's ship recycling, has been modernised and aligned with the Hong Kong International Convention (HKC), which became mandatory from 26 June 2025, backed by a legal framework comprising the Ship Recycling Act 2019, Rules 2021, and Regulations 2026.

title: Implementation of Anemia Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan Operational Guidelines

ministry.name: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

summary: The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has released Operational Guidelines for the Anemia Mukt Bharat (AMB) Abhiyaan, introducing an upgraded '7X7X7' framework that replaces the earlier '6X6X6' strategy. The new framework covers seven beneficiary groups, seven interventions, and seven institutional mechanisms, with a shift from the 'T3' (Test, Treat, Talk) approach to a 'T4' approach (Test, Treat, Talk and Track) for digital monitoring. This was stated by Union Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare, Smt. Anupriya Patel, in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha on 11 August 2026.

title: Steps Taken to Promote Menstrual Health and Hygiene

ministry.name: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

summary: In a written Rajya Sabha reply, Union Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare Anupriya Patel outlined steps taken to promote menstrual health and hygiene in India. These include the Menstrual Hygiene Scheme (MHS) under the National Health Mission (NHM), which supports States/UTs based on their Annual Programme Implementation Plans, and the Menstrual Hygiene Policy for School-going Girls implemented through inter-departmental coordination. Monitoring is done through NPCC meetings and annual Common Review Missions (CRMs).

title: GARMENT EXPORTS
summary: India's textile, apparel and handicrafts exports grew at a CAGR of about 4.5% from ₹2,49,250 crore in 2019-20 to ₹3,25,339 crore in 2025-26, with 1.8% growth over the previous year. Tamil Nadu, Gujarat and Haryana lead among exporting states, while Tiruppur, Gautam Buddha Nagar and Bengaluru Urban top the list of 548 exporting districts. The Ministry of Textiles detailed multiple support schemes including PM MITRA Parks, PLI for Textiles, RoDTEP/RoSCTL extension, FTAs, and sustainability initiatives like Tex-Eco, given in a Lok Sabha written reply.

title: ANCHOR INVESTMENTS AND TEXTILE VALUE-CHAIN
summary: The Ministry of Textiles informed Lok Sabha that under the PM MITRA Parks scheme (outlay Rs. 4,445 crore, 2021-22 to 2027-28), all 7 selected sites across Tamil Nadu, Telangana, Gujarat, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, and Maharashtra have completed MoUs, 100% land acquisition, and environmental clearances. DPRs worth Rs. 13,537 crore have been finalized, and investment interest of Rs. 68,590 crore has been received, with external and internal infrastructure works underway. The Budget 2026-27 also announced a new Mega Textile Parks scheme, for which states will be asked to submit proposals.

title: Steps taken for Promotion and Regulation of Regenerative Medicines

ministry.name: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

summary: In a written Rajya Sabha reply, the Union Health Ministry detailed the regulatory and promotional framework for regenerative medicine in India, listing key guidelines such as the 2025-26 Evidence-Based Guidelines for Stem Cell Therapy, the 2023 Umbilical Cord Blood Banking Guidelines, the 2021 National Guidelines for Hematopoietic Cell Transplantation, the 2019 Gene Therapy Guidelines, and the 2017 National Guidelines for Stem Cell Research.
